name: types

types.name: AgenticConfig
types.description:
AgenticConfig is the configuration for the agentic workstation sensor.
 The daemon receives events from coding-agent hooks (PostToolUse,
 SubagentStart, etc.) via a Unix socket, batches them, and publishes
 to EventBus. From there, Aegis ingests the events for topology
 visualization and forensics.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between event flushes to EventBus. Default: 5000.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max events per flush. Default: 100.

fields.name: max_event_payload_bytes
fields.description:
max_event_payload_bytes caps how much of each tool input/output is
 stored per event. Larger payloads are truncated. Default: 32768 (32KB).

fields.name: file_pattern_excludelist
fields.description:
file_pattern_excludelist is a set of glob patterns for files to
 exclude from tracking. Example: ["*.lock", "node_modules/**", ".git/**"].

fields.name: spool_max_bytes
fields.description:
spool_max_bytes is the maximum spool file size in bytes. When the spool
 reaches this limit, new events are dropped until the backlog drains.
 Default: 524288000 (500MB).

types.name: Config
types.description:
Config is the per-profile configuration for cavalier.
 Loaded from all YAML files in ~/.cavalier/config/ and merged.
 Splitting connection and key into separate files (config.yaml + key.yaml)
 allows chmod 400 on the key file.

fields.name: connection
fields.description:
connection is the gRPC connection configuration.
 Used by the identity manager for token exchange with gateway.
 Contains endpoints, private_key, and trusted_cas.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the single configuration type for all services.

 Bootstrap fields (endpoints, instance_id, private_key, trusted_cas) are loaded
 from YAML at boot and used to connect to the cluster.

 Runtime fields (ping_interval_ms, rebalance_interval_ms, listen_address,
 max_request_size, request_timeout_seconds, logger, shutdown_timeout_seconds)
 are delivered by the cluster via ServiceConfigState and can change at any time.

 TLS certificates are obtained automatically by the servicemanager via X509Mint
 after token exchange — they are not part of the config.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.description:
Cluster endpoints. Set in bootstrap file; can be updated at runtime
 via ServiceConfigState to add/remove endpoints dynamically.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id uniquely identifies this running instance/replica.
 Used for leader elections on boundaries with (spec.leader) = true.
 If empty, a random ID is generated at client creation time.

fields.name: private_key
fields.description:
private_key is used to mint throwaway bootstrap JWTs for the
 token exchange flow. The kid is in private_key.id;
 identity (subject/audience) comes from the delegate looked up
 by TokenExchanger using the matching kid.
 If absent, cloud-native authentication is attempted.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: ping_interval_ms
fields.description:
ping_interval_ms controls how often each endpoint is pinged for latency measurement.
 Default: 5000 (5 seconds)

fields.name: rebalance_interval_ms
fields.description:
rebalance_interval_ms controls how often the active connection is re-evaluated
 based on latency. Default: 10000 (10 seconds)

fields.name: listen_address
fields.description: listen_address is the bind address for the gRPC server. Default port 8443.

fields.name: max_request_size
fields.description:
max_request_size is the maximum request size in bytes.
 Must be greater than 0. Default: 10MB (10485760 bytes)

fields.name: request_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
request_timeout_seconds is the timeout for client requests.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description:
logger configures the logger for the service.
 Controls log format (JSON/console), level, output paths, and more.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_concurrent_streams
fields.description:
max_concurrent_streams limits the number of concurrent gRPC streams per connection.
 Prevents resource exhaustion from clients opening unlimited streams.
 Default: 100. Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default (unlimited).

fields.name: max_send_msg_size
fields.description:
max_send_msg_size is the maximum response message size in bytes.
 Prevents the server from sending responses that could OOM clients.
 Default: 16MB (16777216 bytes). Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default.

fields.name: keepalive_min_time_seconds
fields.description:
keepalive_min_time_seconds is the minimum interval clients must wait between
 keepalive pings. Clients pinging more frequently are disconnected.
 Default: 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable enforcement.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the explicit list of CA certificates trusted for SPIFFE TLS
 verification when connecting to cluster endpoints. It must not be empty.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain).
 It must not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path.
 Service identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on health reports or X509 URI SANs.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this service instance's topology path under /system —
 opaque, tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed
 (e.g. "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the
 SPIFFE segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the
 operator/deployment from runtime config (where the service runs); it is
 not a token claim. May be empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: disk_persistence
fields.description:
disk_persistence is an init-time/bootstrap setting that enables
 ServiceManager-owned redo-log lifecycle for generated service_store stores.
 When present at ServiceManager creation, the generated ServiceManager opens
 the per-store redo logs, exposes those handles to service code, and owns
 scheduled compaction/roll. It is not hot-reloaded; when absent, typed
 diskstore helpers remain available but no managed roll loop is started.

message.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
message.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.name: archive_count
fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.name: dir
fields.description:
dir is the base directory (on the service's own volume) for the
 active / building / temp / archive files.

fields.name: file_permission
fields.description: file_permission is the Unix permission for the data files (e.g. 0600).

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

fields.name: anonymize_hmac_key
fields.description:
anonymize_hmac_key is the per-deployment data-entitlement ANONYMIZE secret:
 the keyed-HMAC key the generated service wrapper supplies to Sanitize<T> so
 a value pseudonymizes to the same surrogate at any depth, across services
 and restarts. Required only by services whose records carry
 ANONYMIZE-capable (spec.redact) fields — the generated pseudonymize
 primitives fail loud on an empty key.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the port for a separate PLAINTEXT gRPC listener that
 serves ONLY grpc.health.v1. k8s kubelet probes are plaintext-only and
 cannot speak TLS, so the main TLS port (listen_address) is invisible to
 them. This listener runs on a completely separate grpc.Server / tonic
 Server / NettyServerBuilder with no TLS, no auth interceptors, and no
 business services registered — isolation is the security argument.
 The health status reflects the same StatusSink-driven state as the TLS
 health endpoint: NOT_SERVING until bootstrap completes, then tracks
 handler health (UNHEALTHY → NOT_SERVING, recovery → SERVING).
 Default: 8444. Set to 0 to disable the plaintext health probe listener.

fields.name: format
fields.description: format is the default output format.

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: JSON format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_YAML
enum_values.description: YAML format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_MULTI_YAML
enum_values.description: Multi YAML format (e.g. ---)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TEXT
enum_values.description: Plain text format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_ENV_VAR
enum_values.description: Environment variable format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE
enum_values.description: Protobuf wire format (binary)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TOML
enum_values.description: TOML format

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the full project namespace this profile logs into
 (e.g. "/cavalier/default"). cavalier is a user/project tool: it does NOT
 do domain lookup — the user specifies which project to authenticate to.
 `cavalier auth` uses this to select the project at login.

fields.name: api_transport
fields.description:
api_transport selects the generated-client transport used through the
 local daemon. Defaults to GRPC; REST is intended for testing and
 troubleshooting.

 Values are "grpc" or "rest".

rpcs.description:
BrokerAuth begins authentication if the daemon has no valid local token.
 The daemon owns the OAuth backend session and returns an auth URL for the
 caller to present or open. Returns immediately if a valid local token
 already exists. BrokerAuth does not wait for browser completion; callers
 that need completion should observe SubscribeStatus.
rpcs.verb_definition: Coordinate a mediated exchange between two parties.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

rpcs.description:
Ping verifies that the local daemon process is alive and serving the
 Unix-socket control plane.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get; liveness/health signal only.

rpcs.description: GetStatus returns daemon health, token state, and version info.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
SubscribeStatus streams daemon health, token state, and version info.
 The server sends the current status immediately, then sends a new
 response whenever the status changes.
rpcs.verb_definition: Open a long-lived domain stream that is not a collection WATCH envelope.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Watch; use Watch only for generated collection snapshot/upsert/delete streams.

rpcs.description:
ResetProxyStats clears accumulated local proxy listener counters.
 Listener definitions and current bind state are preserved.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Update; resets to a defined baseline rather than applying arbitrary changes.

rpcs.description:
GetToken returns an audience-scoped bearer token for direct gRPC calls.
 The daemon mints from its stored refresh token. Triggers auth if needed.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
GetProxyEnv returns the daemon's current proxy environment values
 (local API key, per-provider HTTP base URLs, CA cert path). The cavalier
 CLI uses this to emit `export NAME=VALUE` lines for `source <(cavalier env)`,
 and to populate `~/.claude/settings.json`. Reads from in-memory daemon
 state — no disk file involved.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
GetRefreshToken returns the daemon's in-memory refresh token (empty
 if unauthenticated). Used by the CLI to carry the token across a
 daemon version-restart without re-prompting the user. Filesystem
 permissions on the unix socket are the security boundary.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
UpdateRefreshToken installs a refresh token into the daemon's in-memory
 state (Client IM). Symmetric with GetRefreshToken; used after a
 version-restart to repopulate the new daemon without re-auth.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description: PublishHook accepts a single hook event.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Send; fan-out to topic subscribers.

enums.name: ApiTransport
enums.description:
ApiTransport selects how generated client calls route through the local daemon.
 The zero value is treated as GRPC so existing configs keep the default path.

services.name: DaemonControl
services.description:
DaemonControl is the local IPC interface between the cavalier CLI
 and the background daemon process.

 Transport: Unix socket (~/.cavalier/daemon.sock)
 Auth: None — filesystem permissions are the security boundary.

rpcs.description:
BrokerAuth begins authentication if the daemon has no valid local token.
 The daemon owns the OAuth backend session and returns an auth URL for the
 caller to present or open. Returns immediately if a valid local token
 already exists. BrokerAuth does not wait for browser completion; callers
 that need completion should observe SubscribeStatus.
rpcs.verb_definition: Coordinate a mediated exchange between two parties.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

rpcs.description:
Ping verifies that the local daemon process is alive and serving the
 Unix-socket control plane.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get; liveness/health signal only.

rpcs.description: GetStatus returns daemon health, token state, and version info.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
SubscribeStatus streams daemon health, token state, and version info.
 The server sends the current status immediately, then sends a new
 response whenever the status changes.
rpcs.verb_definition: Open a long-lived domain stream that is not a collection WATCH envelope.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Watch; use Watch only for generated collection snapshot/upsert/delete streams.

rpcs.description:
ResetProxyStats clears accumulated local proxy listener counters.
 Listener definitions and current bind state are preserved.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Update; resets to a defined baseline rather than applying arbitrary changes.

rpcs.description:
GetToken returns an audience-scoped bearer token for direct gRPC calls.
 The daemon mints from its stored refresh token. Triggers auth if needed.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
GetProxyEnv returns the daemon's current proxy environment values
 (local API key, per-provider HTTP base URLs, CA cert path). The cavalier
 CLI uses this to emit `export NAME=VALUE` lines for `source <(cavalier env)`,
 and to populate `~/.claude/settings.json`. Reads from in-memory daemon
 state — no disk file involved.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
GetRefreshToken returns the daemon's in-memory refresh token (empty
 if unauthenticated). Used by the CLI to carry the token across a
 daemon version-restart without re-prompting the user. Filesystem
 permissions on the unix socket are the security boundary.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
UpdateRefreshToken installs a refresh token into the daemon's in-memory
 state (Client IM). Symmetric with GetRefreshToken; used after a
 version-restart to repopulate the new daemon without re-auth.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

services.name: HookReceiver
services.description:
HookReceiver accepts hook events from Claude Code and other tools.
 Events are buffered and flushed to EventBus periodically.

rpcs.description: PublishHook accepts a single hook event.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Send; fan-out to topic subscribers.

types.name: Config
types.description:
Config is the per-invocation configuration for cavalierctl.

 Loaded from a YAML file passed via --config, or assembled entirely from
 CLI flags. Unlike cavalier, there is no $HOME-based config directory —
 the cred_pair private key is treated as a CI secret and is loaded from
 an explicit --key-file path (or stdin via "-", or the
 CAVALIERCTL_KEY_FILE env var).

fields.name: connection
fields.description:
connection is the gRPC connection configuration — endpoints (gateway),
 trusted_cas, and (when loaded by the CLI) the cluster cred_pair
 private key in connection.private_key. The private key is NOT carried
 in the YAML config file; it is loaded separately from --key-file at
 runtime and merged into this message before use.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the single configuration type for all services.

 Bootstrap fields (endpoints, instance_id, private_key, trusted_cas) are loaded
 from YAML at boot and used to connect to the cluster.

 Runtime fields (ping_interval_ms, rebalance_interval_ms, listen_address,
 max_request_size, request_timeout_seconds, logger, shutdown_timeout_seconds)
 are delivered by the cluster via ServiceConfigState and can change at any time.

 TLS certificates are obtained automatically by the servicemanager via X509Mint
 after token exchange — they are not part of the config.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.description:
Cluster endpoints. Set in bootstrap file; can be updated at runtime
 via ServiceConfigState to add/remove endpoints dynamically.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id uniquely identifies this running instance/replica.
 Used for leader elections on boundaries with (spec.leader) = true.
 If empty, a random ID is generated at client creation time.

fields.name: private_key
fields.description:
private_key is used to mint throwaway bootstrap JWTs for the
 token exchange flow. The kid is in private_key.id;
 identity (subject/audience) comes from the delegate looked up
 by TokenExchanger using the matching kid.
 If absent, cloud-native authentication is attempted.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: ping_interval_ms
fields.description:
ping_interval_ms controls how often each endpoint is pinged for latency measurement.
 Default: 5000 (5 seconds)

fields.name: rebalance_interval_ms
fields.description:
rebalance_interval_ms controls how often the active connection is re-evaluated
 based on latency. Default: 10000 (10 seconds)

fields.name: listen_address
fields.description: listen_address is the bind address for the gRPC server. Default port 8443.

fields.name: max_request_size
fields.description:
max_request_size is the maximum request size in bytes.
 Must be greater than 0. Default: 10MB (10485760 bytes)

fields.name: request_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
request_timeout_seconds is the timeout for client requests.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description:
logger configures the logger for the service.
 Controls log format (JSON/console), level, output paths, and more.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_concurrent_streams
fields.description:
max_concurrent_streams limits the number of concurrent gRPC streams per connection.
 Prevents resource exhaustion from clients opening unlimited streams.
 Default: 100. Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default (unlimited).

fields.name: max_send_msg_size
fields.description:
max_send_msg_size is the maximum response message size in bytes.
 Prevents the server from sending responses that could OOM clients.
 Default: 16MB (16777216 bytes). Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default.

fields.name: keepalive_min_time_seconds
fields.description:
keepalive_min_time_seconds is the minimum interval clients must wait between
 keepalive pings. Clients pinging more frequently are disconnected.
 Default: 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable enforcement.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the explicit list of CA certificates trusted for SPIFFE TLS
 verification when connecting to cluster endpoints. It must not be empty.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain).
 It must not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path.
 Service identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on health reports or X509 URI SANs.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this service instance's topology path under /system —
 opaque, tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed
 (e.g. "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the
 SPIFFE segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the
 operator/deployment from runtime config (where the service runs); it is
 not a token claim. May be empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: disk_persistence
fields.description:
disk_persistence is an init-time/bootstrap setting that enables
 ServiceManager-owned redo-log lifecycle for generated service_store stores.
 When present at ServiceManager creation, the generated ServiceManager opens
 the per-store redo logs, exposes those handles to service code, and owns
 scheduled compaction/roll. It is not hot-reloaded; when absent, typed
 diskstore helpers remain available but no managed roll loop is started.

message.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
message.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.name: archive_count
fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.name: dir
fields.description:
dir is the base directory (on the service's own volume) for the
 active / building / temp / archive files.

fields.name: file_permission
fields.description: file_permission is the Unix permission for the data files (e.g. 0600).

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

fields.name: anonymize_hmac_key
fields.description:
anonymize_hmac_key is the per-deployment data-entitlement ANONYMIZE secret:
 the keyed-HMAC key the generated service wrapper supplies to Sanitize<T> so
 a value pseudonymizes to the same surrogate at any depth, across services
 and restarts. Required only by services whose records carry
 ANONYMIZE-capable (spec.redact) fields — the generated pseudonymize
 primitives fail loud on an empty key.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the port for a separate PLAINTEXT gRPC listener that
 serves ONLY grpc.health.v1. k8s kubelet probes are plaintext-only and
 cannot speak TLS, so the main TLS port (listen_address) is invisible to
 them. This listener runs on a completely separate grpc.Server / tonic
 Server / NettyServerBuilder with no TLS, no auth interceptors, and no
 business services registered — isolation is the security argument.
 The health status reflects the same StatusSink-driven state as the TLS
 health endpoint: NOT_SERVING until bootstrap completes, then tracks
 handler health (UNHEALTHY → NOT_SERVING, recovery → SERVING).
 Default: 8444. Set to 0 to disable the plaintext health probe listener.

fields.name: cred_pair_id
fields.description:
cred_pair_id is the id of the cluster cred_pair this invocation
 authenticates as. Used as the `kid` header in the signed JWT
 presented to kernel.Mint.MintClientToken. Must match one of
 kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs[*].id on the target cluster.

fields.name: format
fields.description:
format is the default output format for command results (tenant
 listings, etc.). Overridable per-invocation via --format. Default
 is JSON for machine consumption (cavalierctl is CI-first).

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: JSON format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_YAML
enum_values.description: YAML format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_MULTI_YAML
enum_values.description: Multi YAML format (e.g. ---)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TEXT
enum_values.description: Plain text format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_ENV_VAR
enum_values.description: Environment variable format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE
enum_values.description: Protobuf wire format (binary)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TOML
enum_values.description: TOML format

types.name: CredPair
types.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

types.name: Entitlements
types.description:
Entitlements is a set of SPIFFE URI grants. Each grant is a pattern that
 may contain `*` wildcards on path segments. An action against a resource
 is permitted if the resource's SPIFFE URI matches any grant.

 Example grants:
   spiffe://local/dev/_cluster/services/sentinel   — full sentinel access
   spiffe://local/dev/_cluster/services/argus/*    — any argus RPC
   spiffe://local/dev/_models/anthropic/claude-*   — LLM model scoping

 A tenant's own subtree (spiffe://<prefix>/<tenant_name>/...) is implicitly
 granted to all principals inside that tenant and need not be listed.

fields.name: grants
fields.description:
grants is the list of SPIFFE URI patterns this entity is permitted to
 touch. Each pattern may use `*` as a path-segment wildcard.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

types.name: CPSubsystemConfig
types.description:
CPSubsystemConfig configures the consensus-based strong consistency subsystem.
 Used for distributed locks, atomic counters, and leader election.
 Requires an odd number of members (minimum 3) for Raft quorum.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description:
enabled controls whether the CP subsystem is active.
 Must be enabled for distributed locks (Lock service) to work.

fields.name: cp_member_count
fields.description:
cp_member_count is the number of cluster members that participate in
 the CP (consensus protocol) group. Must be odd and >= 3.
 Only these members vote in Raft elections; others are observers.

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is the maximum time a CP session can be inactive
 before it is closed and its resources (locks, etc.) are released.

fields.name: session_heartbeat_interval_seconds
fields.description:
session_heartbeat_interval_seconds is the interval for CP session heartbeats.
 Must be less than session_timeout_seconds.

fields.name: missing_cp_member_auto_removal_seconds
fields.description:
missing_cp_member_auto_removal_seconds is how long to wait before automatically
 removing a missing CP member from the group. Set to 0 to disable auto-removal.

 Legacy format: followed by individual RedoLogEntry records.

types.name: NetworkConfig
types.description: NetworkConfig configures cluster networking behavior.

fields.name: connect_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
connect_timeout_seconds is the maximum time to wait when connecting to a cluster member.
 Default: 5 seconds.

fields.name: heartbeat_interval_seconds
fields.description:
heartbeat_interval_seconds is the interval between heartbeat messages sent to cluster members.
 Used to detect failed nodes.

fields.name: heartbeat_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
heartbeat_timeout_seconds is the time after which a member is considered unreachable
 if no heartbeat is received. Must be greater than heartbeat_interval_seconds.

types.name: PersistenceDump
types.description:
PersistenceDump is a full snapshot of all registered IMaps.
 Written as a single length-prefixed record in dump files.

message.name: PersistenceEntry
message.description:
PersistenceEntry is a typed mutation entry for redo logs and full dumps.
 Replaces the former KitchenSink oneof envelope with google.protobuf.Any
 so that any proto message can be persisted without code generation.

types.name: PersistenceEntry
types.description:
PersistenceEntry is a typed mutation entry for redo logs and full dumps.
 Replaces the former KitchenSink oneof envelope with google.protobuf.Any
 so that any proto message can be persisted without code generation.

types.name: RateLimitConfig
types.description:
RateLimitConfig configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.
 Two categories are tracked independently:
 - polling_rate: unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives (Watch/Subscribe)
 - unary_rate: unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives

fields.name: polling_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives.

fields.name: unary_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives.

types.name: RedoLogEntry
types.description:
RedoLogEntry is a single mutation recorded in the redo log.
 Legacy format: value stored as opaque bytes, requires a parser to deserialize.

enums.name: OpType
enums.description: OpType identifies the type of mutation in a redo log entry.

enums.name: ConsistencyType
enums.description: ConsistencyType identifies the consistency model for a redo log entry.

enums.name: AdminGraphType
enums.description: AdminGraphType classifies a graph boundary.

types.name: AccountingMethod
types.description:
AccountingMethod identifies which RPC an event relates to.
 Only one field will be set — the rest default to 0 (UNSPECIFIED)
 and are not encoded by proto3, so there is no overhead.

RecordMeta
