enums.name: ServiceName
enums.description:
ServiceName provides type-safe service references for S2S authorization.
 Enum values use stable service IDs from explicit service declarations.

enums.name: AgentsensorRPCs
enums.description: agentsensor (vservice, hosted by eventbus)

types.name: Services

fields.name: health_poll_interval_seconds
fields.description: How often to refresh health state (seconds). Default 5.

fields.name: enable_http
fields.description: Enable HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_http3
fields.description: Enable HTTP/3 listener (QUIC/UDP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_grpc
fields.description: Enable gRPC listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: tcp_listener
fields.description: TCP listener for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC. Default port 8443.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: quic_listener
fields.description: QUIC/UDP listener for HTTP/3. Default port 8443.

fields.name: external_tls_mode
fields.description: external_tls_mode controls how the public-facing TLS certificate is provisioned.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_CERT_CHAIN
enum_values.description: CERT_CHAIN: use the cert and key supplied in external_cert_pem / external_key_pem.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_LETSENCRYPT
enum_values.description:
LETSENCRYPT: obtain and renew the certificate automatically via LetsEncrypt.
 Gateway subscribes RO to LetsEncryptState for the current cert.

fields.name: external_hostnames
fields.description:
external_hostnames lists the domain names gateway serves externally.
 Used for SNI-based cert selection at runtime. In LETSENCRYPT mode,
 letsencrypt.Config.hostnames must match this list.

fields.name: external_cert_pem
fields.description:
external_cert_pem is the PEM-encoded certificate chain for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: external_key_pem
fields.description:
external_key_pem is the PEM-encoded private key for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description:
root_ca holds the root CA certificate(s) that clients should trust when
 connecting to the gateway's external HTTPS endpoint. Served via PublicCa
 so clients (cavalierctl, webapp) can configure TLS trust automatically.
 Required in CERT_CHAIN mode. Omit in LETSENCRYPT mode (publicly trusted).

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: lets_encrypt_email
fields.description:
lets_encrypt_email is the email address for Let's Encrypt account
 registration and certificate expiration notifications.
 If empty, letsencrypt will use "admin@<fqdn>".
 NOTES: needs email assertion

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the HTTP server used for ACME HTTP-01
 challenge responses. Must be reachable on port 80 from the internet.
 Default port 80.

fields.name: renewal_check_interval_seconds
fields.description:
renewal_check_interval_seconds is how often to check if the certificate
 needs renewal (seconds). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: hostnames
fields.description:
hostnames is the list of domain names to include as SANs on the
 Let's Encrypt certificate (e.g. ["api.cavalier.io", "console.cavalier.io"]).
 All hostnames must be reachable on port 80 for HTTP-01 challenge validation.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the service-level configuration for graphdb.
 Node mode is determined by the NODE_MODE env var, not by this config.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ZERO
enum_values.description: Zero: cluster management, shard assignment, leader election.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ALPHA
enum_values.description: Alpha: data storage, serves GraphQL/DQL queries.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Zero and Alpha in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: zero_count
fields.description:
zero_count is the expected number of Zero nodes in the cluster.
 Zeros use this to form the Raft quorum. Default: 1.

fields.name: replicas
fields.description:
replicas is the number of Alpha replicas per data shard group.
 Used by Zero nodes.

fields.name: alpha_count
fields.description: alpha_count is the expected number of Alpha nodes. Default: 1.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the ClickHouse materialized view retention. Default: 90.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max rows per insert batch. Default: 10000.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between flushes. Default: 1000.

fields.name: keeper_count
fields.description: keeper_count is the expected number of Keeper nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: data_count
fields.description: data_count is the expected number of Data nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_KEEPER
enum_values.description: Keeper: consensus/coordination (replaces ZooKeeper).

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_DATA
enum_values.description: Data: data storage, serves queries over HTTPS.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Keeper and Data in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

message.name: ProviderConfig
message.description: ProviderConfig configures a single OAuth2 identity provider.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Google", "Okta", "Microsoft").

fields.name: domains
fields.description:
domains maps email domains to this provider. When a user's email domain
 matches, they are routed to this IDP automatically.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the OpenID Connect issuer URL.
 Used for .well-known/openid-configuration auto-discovery.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret.

fields.name: authorization_endpoint
fields.description: authorization_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered authorization URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: token_endpoint
fields.description: token_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered token URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: end_session_endpoint
fields.description: end_session_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered logout URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: scopes overrides the default scopes for this provider.

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description:
ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for this provider.
 Used for providers with self-signed or private CA certificates (e.g. mock IDPs).
 If empty, the system default CA bundle is used.

fields.name: nonce_expire_seconds
fields.description:
nonce_expire_seconds is how long OAuth2 nonces/state remain valid.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks in the authorization code flow.
 Minimum: 1 second. Maximum: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: jwk_refetch_interval_seconds
fields.description:
jwk_refetch_interval_seconds is the minimum interval between JWKS fetches
 from the same external IDP. Prevents excessive outbound requests.
 Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: provider
fields.description: provider selects the messaging platform backend.

fields.name: bot_token
fields.description:
bot_token is the platform bot token for API calls.
 Injected by cavalier.

fields.name: app_token
fields.description:
app_token is the platform app-level token for WebSocket connections
 (e.g., Slack Socket Mode). Injected by cavalier.

fields.name: api_endpoint
fields.description:
api_endpoint is the messaging platform API endpoint.
 Set automatically based on provider if not specified.

fields.name: workspace_id
fields.description: workspace_id is the platform workspace identifier for validation.

fields.name: reconnect_delay_seconds
fields.description:
reconnect_delay_seconds is the delay before reconnecting after a
 WebSocket disconnect. Default: 5 seconds.

fields.name: max_message_length
fields.description:
max_message_length is the maximum message length in characters.
 Slack's limit is 40000 but shorter messages are more readable.

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description:
entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.
 Loaded from services/opa/ by cavalier, delivered to opa via config push.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description:
proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.
 The policy receives caller claims and opaque routing metadata, returns
 an allow/deny decision plus the resolved destination URL.

fields.name: tenant_entitlements_policies
fields.description:
tenant_entitlements_policies holds one entitlements policy per project
 namespace (full path, e.g. "/local/dev/drpepper"). Kernel reconciles each
 tenant_config's OpaTenantConfig into this list; EvalEntitlement dispatches
 on the caller's namespace, falling back to entitlements_policy (cluster
 root) when absent. (repeated-entry, not map<> — map<> round-trips badly
 through tacplus codegen; matches the repeated-entry convention elsewhere.)

message.name: NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy
message.description:
NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy binds a project namespace to its entitlements
 policy bundle — a repeated (map-like) entry used in opa Config/OpaState.

fields.name: hazelcast_memory_mb
fields.description: hazelcast_memory_mb is the Hazelcast cluster memory limit in MB. Default: 2048.

fields.name: map_idle_ttl_seconds
fields.description: map_idle_ttl_seconds evicts idle working-set maps. Default: 7200 (2h).

fields.name: max_maps
fields.description: max_maps limits concurrent working-set maps. Default: 20.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the number of days to retain hot events. Default: 90.

fields.name: cleanup_interval_seconds
fields.description: cleanup_interval_seconds is how often the retention cleanup job runs. Default: 3600.

fields.name: active_session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
active_session_idle_seconds is the idle threshold for ListActiveSessions.
 A session is considered active if its last event was within this window.
 Default: 900 (15 min). Min: 30.

fields.name: scratchpad_ttl_seconds
fields.description: scratchpad_ttl_seconds evicts idle scratchpad entries. 0 = durable (no TTL).

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description:
entity_id is the globally unique URI that identifies this SAML entity.
 It appears in the EntityDescriptor and in every assertion we issue.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com/saml"
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: base_url
fields.description:
base_url is the public HTTPS base URL of this service.
 Used to construct ACS, SSO, SLO, and metadata endpoint URLs.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com"
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: idp_providers
fields.description: idp_providers is the list of external IDP configurations for inbound flows.

message.name: IdpConfig
message.description: IdpConfig configures a single external IDP for inbound SAML flows (SP role).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this IDP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Okta", "Azure AD").

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the IDP's SAML entity ID (must match the Issuer element).

fields.name: metadata_url
fields.description:
metadata_url is the URL of the IDP's SAML EntityDescriptor XML.
 When set, the signing cert is fetched from this URL at startup.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: signing_cert_pem
fields.description:
signing_cert_pem is a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate used to verify
 assertion signatures from this IDP. If metadata_url is set, this is
 derived from the metadata. At least one of these must be provided.

fields.name: acs_path
fields.description:
acs_path is the relative path of our ACS endpoint for this IDP.
 Example: "/saml/acs/okta"
 Defaults to "/saml/acs" if empty.

fields.name: attribute_map
fields.description:
attribute_map maps IDP attribute names to Cavalier claim names.
 Keys are SAML attribute names (e.g. "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress").
 Values are the Cavalier claim names to pass to kernel (e.g. "email").
 If the "email" key is absent after mapping, the NameID is used as the subject.

fields.name: domains
fields.description: domains maps email domains to this IDP. Used for IDP selection hints.

fields.name: sp_providers
fields.description: sp_providers is the list of external SP configurations for outbound flows.

message.name: SpConfig
message.description: SpConfig configures a single external SP for outbound SAML flows (IDP role).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this SP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "AWS Console", "Salesforce").

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the SP's SAML entity ID (used as the Audience).

fields.name: acs_url
fields.description: acs_url is the SP's AssertionConsumerService URL where we POST the assertion.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: name_id_format
fields.description:
name_id_format is the SAML NameID format to use in issued assertions.
 Defaults to emailAddress if empty.

fields.name: attribute_map
fields.description:
attribute_map maps Cavalier claim names to SAML attribute names to include
 in issued assertions. Keys are Cavalier token claims; values are SAML attribute names.

fields.name: want_signed_authn_request
fields.description: want_signed_authn_request indicates whether this SP requires signed AuthnRequests.

fields.name: assertion_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
assertion_lifetime_seconds is how long issued SAML assertions remain valid.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: metadata_cache_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
metadata_cache_ttl_seconds is how long remote IDP metadata is cached.
 Default: 3600 (1 hour).

message.name: Config
message.description:
OperatorConfig is the top-level operator configuration.

 Lifecycle:
   1. operator init ca                   — generate root CA → crypto.yaml
   2. operator init cluster --ca <path>  — generate cluster PKI + write operator.yaml
   3. operator                           — run (IN_CLUSTER) or generate charts (GENERATE_ONLY)

 When deployed to Kubernetes:
   operator.yaml  → ConfigMap  (cavalier-operator-config)
   crypto.yaml    → Secret     (cavalier-operator-crypto)
 Both are mounted and merged by the operator at startup.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: How the operator runs.

enum_values.name: IN_CLUSTER
enum_values.description:
IN_CLUSTER is the default: the operator runs inside Kubernetes and
 continuously reconciles the desired cluster state by managing Helm releases.
 gateway_nodes is automatically set to the number of schedulable nodes.

enum_values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
enum_values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: Public FQDN for the cluster (e.g. "api.example.com").

fields.name: port
fields.description: HTTPS gateway port. Default 443 for production; 8443 for local testing.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Kubernetes namespace to deploy all cavalier services into.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Service replica topology.

message.name: Topology
message.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

 msggateway_nodes is on hold; leave at 0 to disable.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
fields.description: oauth_nodes is used when optional_services.oauth = true (default).

fields.name: msggateway_nodes
fields.description: On hold — leave at 0 to disable.

fields.name: saml_nodes
fields.description: saml_nodes is used when optional_services.saml = true.

fields.name: kmaker_nodes
fields.description:
kmaker_nodes is the number of bootstrap certificate authority replicas.
 Kernel instances contact kmaker with Kubernetes projected service account
 tokens to obtain kernel certificates before kernel itself is available.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
TLS configuration — letsencrypt or custom CA.
 Validation: if tls.letsencrypt = false, tls.ca must be set.

message.name: TLSConfig
message.description:
TLSConfig controls how edge-facing TLS certificates are obtained.
 When letsencrypt = true, the operator deploys one letsencrypt service replica.

fields.name: letsencrypt
fields.description:
When true, Let's Encrypt is used for edge TLS and one letsencrypt service
 replica is deployed. The gateway must be reachable on port 443 from the
 public internet.
 When false, ca must be populated with a valid CA chain.

fields.name: ca
fields.description:
Custom CA chain for edge TLS certificates.
 Required when letsencrypt = false. Ignored when letsencrypt = true.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: pki
fields.description: PKI material. Loaded from crypto.yaml and merged at runtime.

message.name: PKI
message.description:
PKI holds all PKI material for the cluster.

 root_ca is generated once per organization via 'operator init ca'.
 All other fields are generated per-cluster via 'operator init cluster'.
 PKI material lives in crypto.yaml and is merged into OperatorConfig at
 load time. The crypto.yaml file must be kept secret.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description: Shared root CA across all clusters (cert + private key).

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: Cluster intermediate CA, signed by root_ca.

fields.name: node_tls
fields.description: Per-node TLS server certificates (one per kernel/sentinel replica).

fields.name: node_signing_ca
fields.description: Per-node signing CAs for token issuance (one per kernel replica).

fields.name: edge_tls
fields.description:
Edge TLS certificates for gateway and oauth.
 Not used when tls.letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: edge_signing_ca
fields.description: Edge signing CAs.

fields.name: kmaker_signing_ca
fields.description:
Kmaker signing CA, signed by cluster_ca and constrained to issue only
 kernel bootstrap leaf certificates.

fields.name: optional_services
fields.description: Optional add-on services.

message.name: OptionalServices
message.description: OptionalServices controls which optional services are enabled.

fields.name: anthropic
fields.description: Proxy services — when enabled, one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description: MCP server — one replica when enabled.

fields.name: saml
fields.description:
SAML identity provider bridge — saml_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default.

fields.name: oauth
fields.description:
OAuth2/OIDC broker — oauth_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Enabled by default.

fields.name: keycloak
fields.description:
Keycloak IDP — production identity provider.
 Replaces mockidp. Enabled by default.

fields.name: output_dir
fields.description:
Filesystem path where generated Helm charts are written.
 Only used in GENERATE_ONLY mode. Default: "charts".

fields.name: web_root
fields.description:
Filesystem path to the web UI build, mounted read-only into gateway.
 Leave empty to use the gateway's embedded webapp.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
patch is the service image patch number to deploy.
 When 0 (default), the operator auto-tracks the latest patch and polls the
 registry for upgrades (every hour for stable, every 60s for dev builds).
 When set, the operator pins to that exact patch and does no polling.

fields.name: dev
fields.description:
dev selects dev builds when true, stable builds when false (default).
 Affects both the image tag suffix and the polling interval.

fields.name: gitlab_registry_token
fields.description:
gitlab_registry_token is an OAuth2 personal access token (read_registry scope)
 used to pull images from registry.gitlab.com. When set, the operator creates a
 "gitlab-registry" docker-registry Secret in the cavalier namespace as part of
 the generated Helm chart. Keep this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
SPIFFE trust-domain prefix for identity URIs. Every workload identity is
 formed as `spiffe://${spiffe_prefix}/${service_name}` — this powers token
 subject claims, mTLS URI SANs, and (post-B-end-state) SPIFFE-aware client
 cert verification. Operator propagates this value to kernel's bootstrap
 AND to every service configmap so all components agree on the trust
 domain at boot, without a runtime SCS round-trip.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, loaded from
 operator.yaml. The operator renders them into kernel's Helm-deployed config
 (kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs); kernel installs them into the root
 namespace's TenantConfig so they can provision tenants via TenantAdmin.
 Ordinary C2S CredPairs at the root namespace; only public halves are carried.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

fields.name: cluster_oauth
fields.description:
cluster_oauth holds shared (cluster-level) IDP providers — Google, GitHub, etc.
 Configured once by a cluster admin. Delivered to the oauth service for
 initial token validation; tenant routing happens via ClaimMatcher entries
 in each tenant's OAuthTenantConfig.

message.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
message.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:
ClusterOAuthProvider describes a shared IDP (e.g. Google, GitHub) available
 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. "https://accounts.google.com").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the shared OAuth app client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: kmaker
fields.description:
kmaker owns cluster bootstrap certificate signing for kernel. Operator
 renders this into kmaker's mounted runtime config and owns the Secret that
 carries kmaker.Config.signing_ca.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Cavalier cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the deployment prefix for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs.
 Certificates minted here receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=cavalier, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kmaker's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kmaker.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

types.name: TenantConfig
types.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities

 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
SPIFFE identity
 spiffe_id is the full SPIFFE URI for this instance, built by the owning
 service manager via the generated sys/spiffe helper (service_spiffe_id) —
 never hand-formatted. It is one of the durable materialization points of
 the computed identity (health identity, X509 URI SAN, workload keys).
 Format: spiffe://<trust_domain>/system/<location...>/services/<service>[/workloads/<child>...]
 Service:  spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/identity
 Workload: spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/mud-controller/workloads/agent-42
 Consumers needing the location-agnostic service identity parse it with
 service_path_from_spiffe (the bare label, plus any /workloads suffix).

rpcs.description: GetDashboard returns a real-time overview of all coding-agent activity.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description: ListActiveSessions returns all currently active sessions, paginated.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: GetSessionDetail returns the summary and recent events for one session.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description: GetUserActivity returns recent sessions and aggregate stats for one user.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description: ListSessionSearchResults searches sessions by keyword or SQL fragment.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: SubscribeLiveSessions streams real-time session lifecycle events.
rpcs.verb_definition: Open a long-lived domain stream that is not a collection WATCH envelope.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Watch; use Watch only for generated collection snapshot/upsert/delete streams.

rpcs.description: GetScratchpad retrieves a persistent note by key.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description: UpdateScratchpad stores or overwrites a persistent note.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description: DeleteScratchpad removes a persistent note by key.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Revoke; removes resource state rather than invalidating a credential or grant.

rpcs.description: ListScratchpads lists all stored note keys with metadata.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: DeleteScratchpads removes all stored notes.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Revoke; removes resource state rather than invalidating a credential or grant.

rpcs.description:

rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description: SubscribeDashboard streams dashboard snapshots, pushed every ~2s as session state changes.

rpcs.description: SubscribeUserActivity streams updated activity stats for one user as sessions evolve.

types.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

types.name: ResetConsumerGroupOffsetsRequest
SortField
SubscribeRequest
types.description:
SubscribeRequest is sent on the bidi stream to control replay.
 The first message establishes the session; subsequent messages adjust
 position, speed, pause state, or backpressure without closing the stream.

 Every field is applied as-is — the server replaces its current state
 with the full contents of each new SubscribeRequest. To change only
 the speed, the client re-sends the same seek + the new speed.

fields.name: consumer_group
fields.description:
Consumer group for offset tracking. Only read from the first message;
 ignored on subsequent resubscribes (consumer group is immutable per session).

fields.name: speed_multiplier
fields.description:
speed_multiplier controls replay pacing relative to original event timestamps.
 0 = max throughput (catch-up mode, no delay between events).
 1.0 = real-time (events delivered at the same rate they were produced).
 10.0 = 10x fast-forward.
 Can be changed mid-stream without seeking.

fields.name: pause
fields.description:
pause stops delivery without closing the stream or releasing the consumer.
 The server holds its position. Send pause=false (or a new seek) to resume.

fields.name: backpressure
fields.description: backpressure tells the server what to do when the client is slow.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER: server buffers events until the client catches up.
 Default gRPC behaviour. Safe but risks unbounded memory if the client
 falls behind permanently.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD: server skips ahead to the latest available offset,
 discarding events the client couldn't consume in time. The client sees
 a gap but never falls behind.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE: server delivers every Nth event (N = sample_interval),
 dropping the rest. Useful for dashboards that need shape, not completeness.

values.name: BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER
values.description:

 falls behind permanently.

values.name: BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD
values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD: server skips ahead to the latest available offset,
 discarding events the client couldn't consume in time. The client sees
 a gap but never falls behind.

types.name: Cluster
types.description:
============================================================================
 Cluster State (cluster diagnostics, health, and metrics)
 ============================================================================

 Cluster is a state root that exposes cluster diagnostics and
 operational metrics. A background publisher in each node periodically
 computes metrics from JVM/Hazelcast APIs and writes them to the maps.
 Tacplus auto-generates Get/Set/Watch RPCs for each boundary.

 PATTERNS TO ADDRESS LATER:

 1. Filtered queries: GetMapEntries needs key_prefix filter and limit.
    The auto-generated collection Get doesn't support ad-hoc filtering.
    Needs a hand-wrapped RPC or a new tacplus pattern for parameterized
    queries on collections.

 2. Transient point-in-time queries: ListLocks returns a snapshot of
    lock state that changes too rapidly to publish to maps. Needs a
    hand-wrapped RPC. Same applies to thread deadlock detection —
    better as on-demand than periodic.

 3. Publisher latency vs event-driven updates: Watch fires when maps
    update, but the publisher writes on a fixed interval. For membership
    changes, consider event-driven publishing (MembershipListener
    triggers immediate cluster_info/cluster_health write) alongside
    periodic publishing for metrics.

Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
persistence_dir
fields.description:
persistence_dir is the directory where DB dumps and redo logs are stored.
 Default: "data/kernel".

fields.name: persistence_format
fields.description:
persistence_format configures the serialization format for redo logs and dumps.
 Default: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE (binary protobuf).

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: JSON format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_YAML
enum_values.description: YAML format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_MULTI_YAML
enum_values.description: Multi YAML format (e.g. ---)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TEXT
enum_values.description: Plain text format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_ENV_VAR
enum_values.description: Environment variable format

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_PROTO_WIRE
enum_values.description: Protobuf wire format (binary)

enum_values.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT_TOML
enum_values.description: TOML format

fields.name: hazelcast_listener
fields.description: hazelcast_listener is the bind address for Hazelcast cluster communication. Default port 5001.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the node's X.509 certificate and private key, used for
 gRPC server TLS and Hazelcast mTLS.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description:
cluster_ca holds the cluster root CA certificate(s) for populating
 Ca.ca_certs on startup and for Hazelcast mTLS trust.
 These are the trust anchors for all cert chain validation in the cluster.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the node's intermediate CA chain issued by cavalier,
 used by X509Mint to sign service certificates. The chain is:
   node intermediate (pathlen:0) → cluster intermediate → root CA.
 The private key is included (for signing) but never leaves the node.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description: trusted_cas lists the trusted CA certificates for TLS verification.

fields.name: rate_limit
fields.description: rate_limit configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.

message.name: RateLimitConfig
message.description:
RateLimitConfig configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.
 Two categories are tracked independently:
 - polling_rate: unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives (Watch/Subscribe)
 - unary_rate: unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives

fields.name: polling_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives.

fields.name: unary_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives.

fields.name: configs
fields.description:
configs holds per-service configurations. On each config load,
 each entry is written to the corresponding service config state boundary.

fields.name: health_poll_interval_seconds
fields.description: How often to refresh health state (seconds). Default 5.

fields.name: enable_http
fields.description: Enable HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_http3
fields.description: Enable HTTP/3 listener (QUIC/UDP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_grpc
fields.description: Enable gRPC listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: tcp_listener
fields.description: TCP listener for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC. Default port 8443.

fields.name: quic_listener
fields.description: QUIC/UDP listener for HTTP/3. Default port 8443.

fields.name: external_tls_mode
fields.description: external_tls_mode controls how the public-facing TLS certificate is provisioned.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_CERT_CHAIN
enum_values.description: CERT_CHAIN: use the cert and key supplied in external_cert_pem / external_key_pem.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_LETSENCRYPT
enum_values.description:
LETSENCRYPT: obtain and renew the certificate automatically via LetsEncrypt.
 Gateway subscribes RO to LetsEncryptState for the current cert.

fields.name: external_hostnames
fields.description:
external_hostnames lists the domain names gateway serves externally.
 Used for SNI-based cert selection at runtime. In LETSENCRYPT mode,
 letsencrypt.Config.hostnames must match this list.

fields.name: external_cert_pem
fields.description:
external_cert_pem is the PEM-encoded certificate chain for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: external_key_pem
fields.description:
external_key_pem is the PEM-encoded private key for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description:
root_ca holds the root CA certificate(s) that clients should trust when
 connecting to the gateway's external HTTPS endpoint. Served via PublicCa
 so clients (cavalierctl, webapp) can configure TLS trust automatically.
 Required in CERT_CHAIN mode. Omit in LETSENCRYPT mode (publicly trusted).

fields.name: lets_encrypt_email
fields.description:
lets_encrypt_email is the email address for Let's Encrypt account
 registration and certificate expiration notifications.
 If empty, letsencrypt will use "admin@<fqdn>".
 NOTES: needs email assertion

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the HTTP server used for ACME HTTP-01
 challenge responses. Must be reachable on port 80 from the internet.
 Default port 80.

fields.name: renewal_check_interval_seconds
fields.description:
renewal_check_interval_seconds is how often to check if the certificate
 needs renewal (seconds). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: hostnames
fields.description:
hostnames is the list of domain names to include as SANs on the
 Let's Encrypt certificate (e.g. ["api.cavalier.io", "console.cavalier.io"]).
 All hostnames must be reachable on port 80 for HTTP-01 challenge validation.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is the service-level configuration for graphdb.
 Node mode is determined by the NODE_MODE env var, not by this config.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ZERO
enum_values.description: Zero: cluster management, shard assignment, leader election.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_ALPHA
enum_values.description: Alpha: data storage, serves GraphQL/DQL queries.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Zero and Alpha in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: zero_count
fields.description:
zero_count is the expected number of Zero nodes in the cluster.
 Zeros use this to form the Raft quorum. Default: 1.

fields.name: replicas
fields.description:
replicas is the number of Alpha replicas per data shard group.
 Used by Zero nodes.

fields.name: alpha_count
fields.description: alpha_count is the expected number of Alpha nodes. Default: 1.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the ClickHouse materialized view retention. Default: 90.

fields.name: batch_size
fields.description: batch_size is the max rows per insert batch. Default: 10000.

fields.name: flush_interval_ms
fields.description: flush_interval_ms is the max time between flushes. Default: 1000.

fields.name: keeper_count
fields.description: keeper_count is the expected number of Keeper nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: data_count
fields.description: data_count is the expected number of Data nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is the role assigned to this node.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_KEEPER
enum_values.description: Keeper: consensus/coordination (replaces ZooKeeper).

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_DATA
enum_values.description: Data: data storage, serves queries over HTTPS.

enum_values.name: NODE_MODE_COMBINED
enum_values.description: Combined: runs both Keeper and Data in a single container (dev only).

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

message.name: ProviderConfig
message.description: ProviderConfig configures a single OAuth2 identity provider.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Google", "Okta", "Microsoft").

fields.name: domains
fields.description:
domains maps email domains to this provider. When a user's email domain
 matches, they are routed to this IDP automatically.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the OpenID Connect issuer URL.
 Used for .well-known/openid-configuration auto-discovery.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret.

fields.name: authorization_endpoint
fields.description: authorization_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered authorization URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: token_endpoint
fields.description: token_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered token URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: end_session_endpoint
fields.description: end_session_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered logout URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: scopes overrides the default scopes for this provider.

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description:
ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for this provider.
 Used for providers with self-signed or private CA certificates (e.g. mock IDPs).
 If empty, the system default CA bundle is used.

fields.name: nonce_expire_seconds
fields.description:
nonce_expire_seconds is how long OAuth2 nonces/state remain valid.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks in the authorization code flow.
 Minimum: 1 second. Maximum: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: jwk_refetch_interval_seconds
fields.description:
jwk_refetch_interval_seconds is the minimum interval between JWKS fetches
 from the same external IDP. Prevents excessive outbound requests.
 Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: provider
fields.description: provider selects the messaging platform backend.

fields.name: bot_token
fields.description:
bot_token is the platform bot token for API calls.
 Injected by cavalier.

fields.name: app_token
fields.description:
app_token is the platform app-level token for WebSocket connections
 (e.g., Slack Socket Mode). Injected by cavalier.

fields.name: api_endpoint
fields.description:
api_endpoint is the messaging platform API endpoint.
 Set automatically based on provider if not specified.

fields.name: workspace_id
fields.description: workspace_id is the platform workspace identifier for validation.

fields.name: reconnect_delay_seconds
fields.description:
reconnect_delay_seconds is the delay before reconnecting after a
 WebSocket disconnect. Default: 5 seconds.

fields.name: max_message_length
fields.description:
max_message_length is the maximum message length in characters.
 Slack's limit is 40000 but shorter messages are more readable.

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description:
entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.
 Loaded from services/opa/ by cavalier, delivered to opa via config push.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description:
proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.
 The policy receives caller claims and opaque routing metadata, returns
 an allow/deny decision plus the resolved destination URL.

fields.name: tenant_entitlements_policies
fields.description:
tenant_entitlements_policies holds one entitlements policy per project
 namespace (full path, e.g. "/local/dev/drpepper"). Kernel reconciles each
 tenant_config's OpaTenantConfig into this list; EvalEntitlement dispatches
 on the caller's namespace, falling back to entitlements_policy (cluster
 root) when absent. (repeated-entry, not map<> — map<> round-trips badly
 through tacplus codegen; matches the repeated-entry convention elsewhere.)

message.name: NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy
message.description:
NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy binds a project namespace to its entitlements
 policy bundle — a repeated (map-like) entry used in opa Config/OpaState.

fields.name: hazelcast_memory_mb
fields.description: hazelcast_memory_mb is the Hazelcast cluster memory limit in MB. Default: 2048.

fields.name: map_idle_ttl_seconds
fields.description: map_idle_ttl_seconds evicts idle working-set maps. Default: 7200 (2h).

fields.name: max_maps
fields.description: max_maps limits concurrent working-set maps. Default: 20.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the number of days to retain hot events. Default: 90.

fields.name: cleanup_interval_seconds
fields.description: cleanup_interval_seconds is how often the retention cleanup job runs. Default: 3600.

fields.name: active_session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
active_session_idle_seconds is the idle threshold for ListActiveSessions.
 A session is considered active if its last event was within this window.
 Default: 900 (15 min). Min: 30.

fields.name: scratchpad_ttl_seconds
fields.description: scratchpad_ttl_seconds evicts idle scratchpad entries. 0 = durable (no TTL).

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description:
entity_id is the globally unique URI that identifies this SAML entity.
 It appears in the EntityDescriptor and in every assertion we issue.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com/saml"
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: base_url
fields.description:
base_url is the public HTTPS base URL of this service.
 Used to construct ACS, SSO, SLO, and metadata endpoint URLs.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com"
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: idp_providers
fields.description: idp_providers is the list of external IDP configurations for inbound flows.

message.name: IdpConfig
message.description: IdpConfig configures a single external IDP for inbound SAML flows (SP role).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this IDP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Okta", "Azure AD").

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the IDP's SAML entity ID (must match the Issuer element).

fields.name: metadata_url
fields.description:
metadata_url is the URL of the IDP's SAML EntityDescriptor XML.
 When set, the signing cert is fetched from this URL at startup.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: signing_cert_pem
fields.description:
signing_cert_pem is a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate used to verify
 assertion signatures from this IDP. If metadata_url is set, this is
 derived from the metadata. At least one of these must be provided.

fields.name: acs_path
fields.description:
acs_path is the relative path of our ACS endpoint for this IDP.
 Example: "/saml/acs/okta"
 Defaults to "/saml/acs" if empty.

fields.name: attribute_map
fields.description:
attribute_map maps IDP attribute names to Cavalier claim names.
