custom_claims are static key-value pairs added to every access token
 minted for this delegate. Useful for identity claims (e.g. email).
 Standard JWT claims (sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, azp, nbf, jti, typ,
 parent_sub) are reserved and will be skipped.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the fully qualified domain name for this cluster
 (e.g. "api.example.com"). Published to Identity state for
 services like letsencrypt. No default — must be set for production.
constraints: must be a fully qualified domain name

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the full issuer URL for tokens minted by this cluster.
 For local development, computed as https://<fqdn>:<port> (port omitted if 443).
 For production behind a load balancer, set explicitly (e.g. "https://api.example.com").

fields.name: key_rotation_interval_seconds
fields.description:
key_rotation_interval_seconds is how often the exchanger rotates
 its own signing keys. Default: 24 hours.

fields.name: default_token_expiry_seconds
fields.description:
default_token_expiry_seconds is the default lifetime for issued
 access tokens when the request does not specify an expiry. Default: 1 hour.

fields.name: ca_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
ca_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for node CA certificates.
 Default: 31536000 (1 year). Node CA certs are regenerated on restart.

fields.name: access_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
access_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user access tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 900 (15 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user refresh tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: tls_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
tls_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for auto-TLS service certificates.
 Kernel sends a renewal request at half-life. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: max_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
max_token_lifetime_seconds is the maximum lifetime kernel will allow for
 any minted token. Requests with exp beyond now + this value are rejected.
 Delegates control their own exp policy within this ceiling.
 Default: 2592000 (30 days).

fields.name: offline_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
offline_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for Offline Tokens
 (OT) — the long-lived, identity-only tokens persisted on disk by the
 cavalier daemon and renewed before half-life. Months, not hours.
 Default: 7776000 (90 days). Exempt from max_token_lifetime_seconds, which
 caps short-lived access/service tokens.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, rendered into this
 config by the operator from operator.yaml. Each is an ordinary C2S CredPair
 owned by the root namespace; kernel installs them into the root namespace's
 TenantConfig at boot (granting full entitlements) so a holder can sign a
 proof, exchange it via MintClientToken, and provision tenants/projects via
 TenantAdmin. Only the public half is carried here.

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain). It must
 not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path. Service
 identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on issued tokens or X509 URI SANs. Kernel
 copies this (with location_path) into the runtime grpcconfig.Config it seeds
 into ServiceConfigState, so every service shares one trust domain.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this deployment's topology path under /system — opaque,
 tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed (e.g.
 "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the SPIFFE
 segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the operator from
 runtime config (where the cluster runs); it is not a token claim. May be
 empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kernel's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kernel.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

types.name: ConfigState
types.description:
ConfigState is the kernel-hosted persistence boundary for tenants/projects.
 Kernel writes it and persists it; other services watch their per-tenant/
 per-project config slice via the export: true wire.

fields.name: tenants
fields.description: tenants is the list of all tenant records, keyed by tenant.name.

message.name: Tenant
message.description:

   spiffe://<trust-domain>/tenants/<name>/...

fields.name: constraints
fields.description:
constraints is the ancestor-set limits (entitlements ceiling now; domain
 later). Set at creation; mutable only by an ancestor.

message.name: Constraints
message.description:
Constraints are the limits an ancestor places on a tenant. They live on the
 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own
 limits. Validated on CreateTenant and SetTenantConfig.

 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: tenant_configs
fields.description: tenant_configs stores each tenant's TenantConfig, keyed by tenant_name.

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities

 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

fields.name: project_configs
fields.description:
project_configs records projects, keyed by the full project namespace
 ("/tenant/project"). ProjectConfig is empty for now (existence only).

message.name: ProjectConfigEntry
message.description:
ProjectConfigEntry maps a full project namespace ("/tenant/project") to its
 (currently empty) ProjectConfig. TenantAdmin writes these.

message.name: ProjectConfig
message.description:
ProjectConfig is a project's configuration. EMPTY for now — its presence
 records the project's existence. Per-project settings will be added later.
 (IDP/OPA live at the tenant, not here.)

types.name: Constraints
types.description:
Constraints are the limits an ancestor places on a tenant. They live on the
 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own
 limits. Validated on CreateTenant and SetTenantConfig.

 (The "min-admin-credential" rule — config must always contain >=1 cred_pair
 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

fields.name: entitlements_ceiling
fields.description:
entitlements_ceiling is the maximum set of entitlements anyone inside this
 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

types.name: Delegate
types.description:
Delegate holds bootstrap matchers for a service or machine client that can request tokens.
 Each delegate is identified by name, which becomes the service path segment in
 the issued token's SPIFFE URI:
 spiffe://<trust-domain>/system/<location>/services/<delegate_name>.
 Authenticates via a projected Kubernetes service-account token or cloud identity.

 Two authorization models:
   - S2S (identity-only): tokens carry only the SPIFFE URI as sub.
     Receiving services enforce access via auth_services RE2 patterns
     that match against the caller's service path.
   - C2S (entitlement-based): OPA returns TokenEntitlements directly.
     Kernel embeds expanded per-service RPC lists in the user token.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is the delegate's identity — becomes the final service path segment in
 the SPIFFE URI. For workload children: parent/<child>.

message.name: CloudIdentityMatcher
message.description:
CloudIdentityMatcher configures which cloud identities a delegate accepts.
 The delegate proves identity using a CloudIdentityProof; this config
 tells kernel what to expect.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: vendor identifies the cloud provider.

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AWS
enum_values.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AZURE
enum_values.description: Microsoft Azure

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_GCP
enum_values.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ORACLE
enum_values.description: Oracle Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ALIBABA
enum_values.description: Alibaba Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_IBM
enum_values.description: IBM Cloud

fields.name: expected_identity
fields.description:
expected_identity is the cloud identity to match against.
 AWS: IAM role ARN. GCP: service account email. Azure: managed identity client ID.

fields.name: kubernetes_service_accounts
fields.description:
kubernetes_service_accounts lists the Kubernetes (namespace, service
 account) pairs that authenticate as this delegate via a projected SA
 token.

message.name: KubernetesServiceAccountMatcher
message.description:
KubernetesServiceAccountMatcher configures which Kubernetes service accounts
 a delegate accepts. The workload proves identity with a projected
 service-account token; this config tells kernel which (namespace, service
 account) pairs map to this delegate. Repeated on Delegate so multiple SAs
 (multi-namespace / migration) can map to one delegate.

fields.name: kubernetes_namespace
fields.description:
kubernetes_namespace is the Kubernetes namespace of the service account.
 Named explicitly to avoid collision with the Cavalier tenant namespace
 concept — this is the K8s namespace, not an authorization namespace.

fields.name: kubernetes_service_account
fields.description: kubernetes_service_account is the Kubernetes ServiceAccount name.

fields.name: authorized_services
fields.description:
authorized_services lists services this delegate can request tokens for.
 Values are generated ServiceName enum entries matching service declarations.
 The delegate can always request a token for itself (sub=name).
 Use SERVICE_NAME_ANY to allow all services.

fields.name: custom_claims
fields.description:
custom_claims are static key-value pairs added to every access token
 minted for this delegate. Useful for identity claims (e.g. email).
 Standard JWT claims (sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, azp, nbf, jti, typ,
 parent_sub) are reserved and will be skipped.

types.name: Identity
types.description:
Identity holds the public verifying keys for kernel's token exchange service.
 Kernel is the sole token authority — all tokens (S2S, U2S, refresh) and
 X.509 certificates are signed by kernel's keys.

 Token exchange handles:
   1. Direct exchange: delegate presents cred_pair JWT or cloud proof → token/cert
   2. Delegation: broker (oauth, K8S) authenticates via header, mints on behalf

 Access: RW for kernel, RO for any service that needs to verify tokens.

fields.name: verifying_keys
fields.description:
Verification keys — kernel's public keys, rotated periodically.
 Kernel holds the corresponding private keys internally.
 Used by SecurityInterceptor to validate tokens for cluster calls.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the cluster's public hostname, published from Config on
 each config load. Services (e.g. letsencrypt) watch this to discover
 the cluster FQDN without needing it in their own config.

message.name: IdentityFqdn
message.description:
IdentityFqdn wraps the cluster's FQDN for publication as a singleton
 boundary in Identity state.

SPIFFE identity

 service manager via the generated sys/spiffe helper (service_spiffe_id) —
 never hand-formatted. It is one of the durable materialization points of
 the computed identity (health identity, X509 URI SAN, workload keys).

 service_path_from_spiffe (the bare label, plus any /workloads suffix).

types.name: KernelDiskState
types.description:
============================================================================
 Kernel disk persistence (UC1 whole-state snapshot)
 ============================================================================

 KernelDiskState is kernel's OWN durable state, snapshotted to kernel's local
 volume via the tacplus diskstore. It is a service_store with NO store_key,
 so tacplus generates UC1 snapshot save/load only (no distributed key-value
 service, no redo log) — kernel persists its whole (small) state as one
 atomic object and restores it on boot.

 Kernel persists ONLY its own state — never another service's. Ephemeral,
 rebuilt-at-runtime state (Cluster membership, ServiceHealth, Identity.fqdn,
 WorkloadState.localities, TrustedCa from Config) is deliberately NOT
 snapshotted; only state that must survive a restart is.

SigningKeyRecord pairs a private signing key with its public JWK so the key
 can be fully restored on restart without re-derivation. Carried inside
 KernelDiskState (the UC1 disk snapshot), one record per active algorithm
 (EdDSA / ES256).

 (The "min-admin-credential" rule — config must always contain >=1 cred_pair
 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

fields.name: entitlements_ceiling
fields.description:
entitlements_ceiling is the maximum set of entitlements anyone inside this
 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:

 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: ProjectConfig
message.description:

message.name: WorkloadRevocation

fields.description: kubernetes_service_account is the Kubernetes ServiceAccount name.

types.name: ServiceHealth
types.description:
ServiceHealth is a state root for service instance health.
 All microservices have RW access. The server enforces per-instance write
 isolation via the token's instance_id claim (instance_keyed annotation).

fields.name: instances
fields.description:
instances holds health data for each running service instance.
 Keyed by "service_id@instance_id" (composed by server from token claims).
 Entries TTL-expire in 30s if not refreshed, ensuring stale instances
 are removed when a process dies.

message.name: ServiceInstanceHealth
message.description:
ServiceInstanceHealth captures the health, load, and reachability of a
 single running instance of a microservice. The composite key
 "service_id@instance_id" is set by the server from the caller's token claims.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Composite key: "service:fleetwood@uuid" — set by server from token claims

fields.name: grpc_endpoint
fields.description: Reachability

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Health

fields.name: cpu_usage
fields.description: Load (auto-collected from runtime)

fields.name: active_requests
fields.description: Load (from grpcserver metrics)

fields.name: p50_latency_us
fields.description: Performance (from grpcserver metrics)

fields.name: version
fields.description: Routing metadata

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description: Timestamps

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
SPIFFE identity
 spiffe_id is the full SPIFFE URI for this instance, built by the owning
 service manager via the generated sys/spiffe helper (service_spiffe_id) —
 never hand-formatted. It is one of the durable materialization points of
 the computed identity (health identity, X509 URI SAN, workload keys).
 Format: spiffe://<trust_domain>/system/<location...>/services/<service>[/workloads/<child>...]
 Service:  spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/identity
 Workload: spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/mud-controller/workloads/agent-42
 Consumers needing the location-agnostic service identity parse it with
 service_path_from_spiffe (the bare label, plus any /workloads suffix).

message.name: ProjectConfig
message.description:
ProjectConfig is a project's configuration. EMPTY for now — its presence
 records the project's existence. Per-project settings will be added later.
 (IDP/OPA live at the tenant, not here.)

types.name: SetTenantConfigRequest

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: Tenant
message.description:
Tenant is the core identity record for a tenant in the cluster.
 `name` is unique, immutable, and becomes the tenant's SPIFFE segment:
   spiffe://<trust-domain>/tenants/<name>/...

fields.name: constraints
fields.description:
constraints is the ancestor-set limits (entitlements ceiling now; domain
 later). Set at creation; mutable only by an ancestor.

message.name: Constraints
message.description:
Constraints are the limits an ancestor places on a tenant. They live on the
 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own
 limits. Validated on CreateTenant and SetTenantConfig.

 (The "min-admin-credential" rule — config must always contain >=1 cred_pair
 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

fields.name: entitlements_ceiling
fields.description:
entitlements_ceiling is the maximum set of entitlements anyone inside this
 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: WorkloadLocality
types.description:
WorkloadLocality holds a parent's current locality token.
 Children present this token on refresh to prove they can still reach
 their parent. The parent rotates the token periodically and registers
 it here. The same token is shared by all of the parent's children —
 it proves reachability, not individual identity.

types.name: WorkloadRevocation
types.description:
WorkloadRevocation records a revoked workload identity.
 Kernel checks this on refresh — if the child's SPIFFE ID (or any
 ancestor) appears here, refresh is denied.

types.name: WorkloadRevokeRequest
types.description:
WorkloadRevokeRequest revokes a child workload's identity by SPIFFE ID.
 Only the parent (or an ancestor in the SPIFFE path) can revoke.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: spiffe_id is the child workload's full SPIFFE ID to revoke.

types.name: WorkloadState
types.description:
WorkloadState tracks workload identity lifecycle — localities and revocations.
 Separate from ServiceHealth to keep health focused on operational status.
 All services have RW (for locality registration); kernel enforces that a
 service can only write its own locality entry (keyed by SPIFFE ID).

fields.name: localities
fields.description:
localities holds locality tokens for parent workloads.
 Parents update these periodically. Children present the token on
 refresh to prove they can still reach their parent.
 Keyed by the parent's SPIFFE ID.

message.name: WorkloadLocality
message.description:
WorkloadLocality holds a parent's current locality token.
 Children present this token on refresh to prove they can still reach
 their parent. The parent rotates the token periodically and registers
 it here. The same token is shared by all of the parent's children —
 it proves reachability, not individual identity.

fields.name: revocations
fields.description:
revocations holds revoked workload SPIFFE IDs.
 Kernel checks this on refresh — if the child's SPIFFE ID (or any
 ancestor) appears here, refresh is denied.
 Keyed by SPIFFE ID. TTL: 24h (longer than any token lifetime).

message.name: WorkloadRevocation
message.description:
WorkloadRevocation records a revoked workload identity.
 Kernel checks this on refresh — if the child's SPIFFE ID (or any
 ancestor) appears here, refresh is denied.

rpcs.description:
MintServiceToken — self-mint. An internal service exchanges its Kubernetes
 token / cloud proof (bootstrap) or a kernel-signed refresh/access token for a
 token bearing its OWN identity (sub = caller SPIFFE). Never calls OPA;
 S2S tokens are identity-only. Signs Ed25519.
 auth_disabled: the caller authenticates via credentials in the request body
 (kubernetes_token / cloud_proof / kernel-signed input_token), not a bearer header.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintUserToken — on-behalf-of (AZP). A broker (oauth/saml) presents the
 user's already-IDP-validated claims; kernel runs OPA EvalEntitlement on
 them, then signs a user token with sub = user and azp = the broker's
 identity (the broker attests the claims; kernel trusts azp). Restricted to
 auth brokers. Signs Ed25519.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintToken — exchange (RT→AT→ST). The caller presents a kernel-signed token;
 kernel VERIFIES it and mints the next tier per the 3-tier rules (a refresh
 can't directly mint a service token, etc.). service_auds mints AT + N ST in
 one call. azp is preserved from the presented token onto every issued
 token. Signs Ed25519. This IS the real exchange (replaces the former
 standalone TokenExchange service).
 auth_disabled: the token to exchange is carried in the request body.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:

services.name: Mint
services.description:
Mint is the platform's sole token authority and signing service, hosted by
 kernel — the cluster trust root. Kernel signs all tokens (S2S, U2S, refresh,
 external/WIF) and all X.509 certificates / workload identities. S2S-only
 (gateway fronts the client-reachable methods as C2S); kernel makes no
 off-cluster calls.

 This is the CLEAN consolidated surface (one service, was 4): the former
 kernel.Mint / kernel.MintClient / kernel.ExternalTokenMint / kernel.TokenExchange
 are unified here. azp is set ONCE at MintUserToken (azp = the broker's
 identity) and preserved unchanged through every derived token (AT from RT,
 ST from AT, and any re-mint/exchange via TokenMint).

 Tokens are signed Ed25519 (internal) except MintExternalToken, which signs
 ES256 for WIF assertion verification (Anthropic WIF rejects EdDSA).

rpcs.description:
MintServiceToken — self-mint. An internal service exchanges its Kubernetes
 token / cloud proof (bootstrap) or a kernel-signed refresh/access token for a
 token bearing its OWN identity (sub = caller SPIFFE). Never calls OPA;
 S2S tokens are identity-only. Signs Ed25519.
 auth_disabled: the caller authenticates via credentials in the request body
 (kubernetes_token / cloud_proof / kernel-signed input_token), not a bearer header.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
MintUserToken — on-behalf-of (AZP). A broker (oauth/saml) presents the
 user's already-IDP-validated claims; kernel runs OPA EvalEntitlement on
 them, then signs a user token with sub = user and azp = the broker's
 identity (the broker attests the claims; kernel trusts azp). Restricted to
 auth brokers. Signs Ed25519.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:

 kernel VERIFIES it and mints the next tier per the 3-tier rules (a refresh
 can't directly mint a service token, etc.). service_auds mints AT + N ST in
 one call. azp is preserved from the presented token onto every issued
 token. Signs Ed25519. This IS the real exchange (replaces the former
 standalone TokenExchange service).
 auth_disabled: the token to exchange is carried in the request body.
