services.name: CliTokenBroker
services.description:
============================================================================
 CLI Token Broker — kernel-mediated nonce matching for CLI auth
 ============================================================================

 Each oauth instance opens a BrokerStream on startup. The protocol:
   1. OAuth sends Register (instance_id) — identifies this stream
   2. CLI auth starts: OAuth sends RegisterNonce (nonce)
   3. Browser completes auth: OAuth sends CompleteNonce (nonce, subject, claims)
   4. Kernel matches nonces, mints token, sends TokenDelivery back to the
      oauth instance that registered the nonce
   5. OAuth delivers the token to the CLI over the Session bidi stream

 Nonce registry is in-memory. Kernel restarts clear it (CLI retries).

services.description:
TenantAdmin is kernel's tenant/project control plane. There is no separate
 cluster-admin service: the namespace tree is uniform (ROOT "/" + tenants +
 projects) and every RPC is ordinary C2S, gated by the single generated
 entitlement authorizer, which enforces the level-or-below rule (caller must be
 at-or-above the target namespace) declaratively via each method's

 tenant admin manages its own subtree. Handlers trust the inbound namespace
 strings (authorization already happened in the interceptor).

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the deployment prefix for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs.
 Certificates minted here receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=cavalier, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.

 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

fields.description: provider_index selects which configured provider to use.

fields.name: callback_url
fields.description:
callback_url is where the user is sent after successful authentication.
 This is the originating microservice's URL (e.g. "https://sentinel:9000/").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: session_id
fields.description:
session_id is set when the OAuth flow was initiated by a CLI client.
 If present, the callback handler writes the minted token to OAuthState
 for delivery to the matching bidi stream.

constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.description: code is the authorization code from the IDP.

fields.name: state
fields.description: state is the anti-CSRF state parameter.

types.name: CallbackResponse
types.description: CallbackResponse contains the minted tokens and the callback destination.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.description: refresh_token is the long-lived refresh token signed by kernel.

fields.name: access_token
fields.description: access_token is the short-lived access token for immediate use.

constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

types.name: SessionRequest
types.description: SessionRequest is sent by the client on the bidi stream.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description:
session_id initiates the session (first message on the stream).
 Must be a cryptographically random identifier (min 32 bytes, hex-encoded).

fields.name: offline_access
fields.description:
offline_access requests an Offline Token (OT) for CLI/daemon sessions.
 The OT is delivered in SessionResponse.token and can be persisted by the
 local daemon; access and service tokens remain derived, short-lived, and
 memory-only.

types.name: SessionResponse
types.description: SessionResponse is sent by the server on the bidi stream.

fields.name: token
fields.description:
token delivers a long-lived refresh token to the client.
 Sent when the Callback writes a token to OAuthState (initial
 auth flow), or when the service proactively refreshes in daemon mode.

fields.name: error
fields.description: error signals a terminal error (session timeout, auth failure, etc.).

rpcs.description:
BrokerSession is a bidirectional stream between cavalierctl and OAuth.
 The client sends a session_id, then waits for token delivery.
 OAuth holds the stream open until the Callback handler writes a
 matching token to OAuthState or the session times out.
rpcs.verb_definition: Coordinate a mediated exchange between two parties.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

rpcs.description:
ListProviders returns the configured OAuth2 providers (public info only).
 The webapp calls this to render provider selection buttons.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
Authorize initiates the OAuth2 authorization code flow.
 Creates a nonce/state in memory and returns the IDP redirect URL.
 The caller provides a callback_url for post-auth redirect.
rpcs.verb_definition: Make an authorization decision (no state change).
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Authenticate/Guard; identity/entitlement decision only.

rpcs.description:
MintCallbackTokens handles the OAuth2 authorization code callback from the IDP.
 Exchanges the authorization code for an IDP ID token, validates it
 against the IDP's JWKS, then delegates to kernel's MintUserToken.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description: RevokeSession invalidates the session and optionally redirects to the IDP logout.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; invalidates credential/session/grant semantics without deleting a resource.

rpcs.description:
BrokerCliAuth is called by the webapp when a user is already logged in
 and session_id is in the URL. OAuth forwards the authenticated identity
 to kernel's CliTokenBroker for nonce completion and token minting.
rpcs.verb_definition: Coordinate a mediated exchange between two parties.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

rpcs.description: Singleton: Config

types.name: Config
types.description:
OperatorConfig is the top-level operator configuration.

 Lifecycle:
   1. operator init ca                   — generate root CA → crypto.yaml
   2. operator init cluster --ca <path>  — generate cluster PKI + write operator.yaml
   3. operator                           — run (IN_CLUSTER) or generate charts (GENERATE_ONLY)

 When deployed to Kubernetes:
   operator.yaml  → ConfigMap  (cavalier-operator-config)
   crypto.yaml    → Secret     (cavalier-operator-crypto)
 Both are mounted and merged by the operator at startup.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: How the operator runs.

enum_values.name: IN_CLUSTER
enum_values.description:
IN_CLUSTER is the default: the operator runs inside Kubernetes and
 continuously reconciles the desired cluster state by managing Helm releases.
 gateway_nodes is automatically set to the number of schedulable nodes.

enum_values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
enum_values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: Public FQDN for the cluster (e.g. "api.example.com").

fields.name: port
fields.description: HTTPS gateway port. Default 443 for production; 8443 for local testing.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Kubernetes namespace to deploy all cavalier services into.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Service replica topology.

message.name: Topology
message.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

 msggateway_nodes is on hold; leave at 0 to disable.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
fields.description: oauth_nodes is used when optional_services.oauth = true (default).

fields.name: msggateway_nodes
fields.description: On hold — leave at 0 to disable.

fields.name: saml_nodes
fields.description: saml_nodes is used when optional_services.saml = true.

fields.name: kmaker_nodes
fields.description:
kmaker_nodes is the number of bootstrap certificate authority replicas.
 Kernel instances contact kmaker with Kubernetes projected service account
 tokens to obtain kernel certificates before kernel itself is available.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
TLS configuration — letsencrypt or custom CA.
 Validation: if tls.letsencrypt = false, tls.ca must be set.

message.name: TLSConfig
message.description:
TLSConfig controls how edge-facing TLS certificates are obtained.
 When letsencrypt = true, the operator deploys one letsencrypt service replica.

fields.name: letsencrypt
fields.description:
When true, Let's Encrypt is used for edge TLS and one letsencrypt service
 replica is deployed. The gateway must be reachable on port 443 from the
 public internet.
 When false, ca must be populated with a valid CA chain.

fields.name: ca
fields.description:
Custom CA chain for edge TLS certificates.
 Required when letsencrypt = false. Ignored when letsencrypt = true.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: pki
fields.description: PKI material. Loaded from crypto.yaml and merged at runtime.

message.name: PKI
message.description:
PKI holds all PKI material for the cluster.

 root_ca is generated once per organization via 'operator init ca'.
 All other fields are generated per-cluster via 'operator init cluster'.
 PKI material lives in crypto.yaml and is merged into OperatorConfig at
 load time. The crypto.yaml file must be kept secret.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description: Shared root CA across all clusters (cert + private key).

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: Cluster intermediate CA, signed by root_ca.

fields.name: node_tls
fields.description: Per-node TLS server certificates (one per kernel/sentinel replica).

fields.name: node_signing_ca
fields.description: Per-node signing CAs for token issuance (one per kernel replica).

fields.name: edge_tls
fields.description:
Edge TLS certificates for gateway and oauth.
 Not used when tls.letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: edge_signing_ca
fields.description: Edge signing CAs.

fields.name: kmaker_signing_ca
fields.description:
Kmaker signing CA, signed by cluster_ca and constrained to issue only
 kernel bootstrap leaf certificates.

fields.name: optional_services
fields.description: Optional add-on services.

message.name: OptionalServices
message.description: OptionalServices controls which optional services are enabled.

fields.name: anthropic
fields.description: Proxy services — when enabled, one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description: MCP server — one replica when enabled.

fields.name: saml
fields.description:
SAML identity provider bridge — saml_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default.

fields.name: oauth
fields.description:
OAuth2/OIDC broker — oauth_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Enabled by default.

fields.name: keycloak
fields.description:
Keycloak IDP — production identity provider.
 Replaces mockidp. Enabled by default.

fields.name: output_dir
fields.description:
Filesystem path where generated Helm charts are written.
 Only used in GENERATE_ONLY mode. Default: "charts".

fields.name: web_root
fields.description:
Filesystem path to the web UI build, mounted read-only into gateway.
 Leave empty to use the gateway's embedded webapp.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
patch is the service image patch number to deploy.
 When 0 (default), the operator auto-tracks the latest patch and polls the
 registry for upgrades (every hour for stable, every 60s for dev builds).
 When set, the operator pins to that exact patch and does no polling.

fields.name: dev
fields.description:
dev selects dev builds when true, stable builds when false (default).
 Affects both the image tag suffix and the polling interval.

fields.name: gitlab_registry_token
fields.description:
gitlab_registry_token is an OAuth2 personal access token (read_registry scope)
 used to pull images from registry.gitlab.com. When set, the operator creates a
 "gitlab-registry" docker-registry Secret in the cavalier namespace as part of
 the generated Helm chart. Keep this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
SPIFFE trust-domain prefix for identity URIs. Every workload identity is
 formed as `spiffe://${spiffe_prefix}/${service_name}` — this powers token
 subject claims, mTLS URI SANs, and (post-B-end-state) SPIFFE-aware client
 cert verification. Operator propagates this value to kernel's bootstrap
 AND to every service configmap so all components agree on the trust
 domain at boot, without a runtime SCS round-trip.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, loaded from
 operator.yaml. The operator renders them into kernel's Helm-deployed config
 (kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs); kernel installs them into the root
 namespace's TenantConfig so they can provision tenants via TenantAdmin.
 Ordinary C2S CredPairs at the root namespace; only public halves are carried.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

fields.name: cluster_oauth
fields.description:
cluster_oauth holds shared (cluster-level) IDP providers — Google, GitHub, etc.
 Configured once by a cluster admin. Delivered to the oauth service for
 initial token validation; tenant routing happens via ClaimMatcher entries
 in each tenant's OAuthTenantConfig.

message.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
message.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:
ClusterOAuthProvider describes a shared IDP (e.g. Google, GitHub) available
 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. "https://accounts.google.com").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the shared OAuth app client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: kmaker
fields.description:
kmaker owns cluster bootstrap certificate signing for kernel. Operator
 renders this into kmaker's mounted runtime config and owns the Secret that
 carries kmaker.Config.signing_ca.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Cavalier cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the deployment prefix for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs.
 Certificates minted here receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=cavalier, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kmaker's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kmaker.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

types.name: MapEmpty
OperatorConfigState
types.description:
OperatorConfigState is the state boundary for operator service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.name: Config
message.description:
OperatorConfig is the top-level operator configuration.

 Lifecycle:
   1. operator init ca                   — generate root CA → crypto.yaml
   2. operator init cluster --ca <path>  — generate cluster PKI + write operator.yaml
   3. operator                           — run (IN_CLUSTER) or generate charts (GENERATE_ONLY)

 When deployed to Kubernetes:
   operator.yaml  → ConfigMap  (cavalier-operator-config)
   crypto.yaml    → Secret     (cavalier-operator-crypto)
 Both are mounted and merged by the operator at startup.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: How the operator runs.

enum_values.name: IN_CLUSTER
enum_values.description:
IN_CLUSTER is the default: the operator runs inside Kubernetes and
 continuously reconciles the desired cluster state by managing Helm releases.
 gateway_nodes is automatically set to the number of schedulable nodes.

enum_values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
enum_values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: Public FQDN for the cluster (e.g. "api.example.com").

fields.name: port
fields.description: HTTPS gateway port. Default 443 for production; 8443 for local testing.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Kubernetes namespace to deploy all cavalier services into.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Service replica topology.

message.name: Topology
message.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

 msggateway_nodes is on hold; leave at 0 to disable.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
fields.description: oauth_nodes is used when optional_services.oauth = true (default).

fields.name: msggateway_nodes
fields.description: On hold — leave at 0 to disable.

fields.name: saml_nodes
fields.description: saml_nodes is used when optional_services.saml = true.

fields.name: kmaker_nodes
fields.description:
kmaker_nodes is the number of bootstrap certificate authority replicas.
 Kernel instances contact kmaker with Kubernetes projected service account
 tokens to obtain kernel certificates before kernel itself is available.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
TLS configuration — letsencrypt or custom CA.
 Validation: if tls.letsencrypt = false, tls.ca must be set.

message.name: TLSConfig
message.description:
TLSConfig controls how edge-facing TLS certificates are obtained.
 When letsencrypt = true, the operator deploys one letsencrypt service replica.

fields.name: letsencrypt
fields.description:
When true, Let's Encrypt is used for edge TLS and one letsencrypt service
 replica is deployed. The gateway must be reachable on port 443 from the
 public internet.
 When false, ca must be populated with a valid CA chain.

fields.name: ca
fields.description:
Custom CA chain for edge TLS certificates.
 Required when letsencrypt = false. Ignored when letsencrypt = true.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: pki
fields.description: PKI material. Loaded from crypto.yaml and merged at runtime.

message.name: PKI
message.description:
PKI holds all PKI material for the cluster.

 root_ca is generated once per organization via 'operator init ca'.
 All other fields are generated per-cluster via 'operator init cluster'.
 PKI material lives in crypto.yaml and is merged into OperatorConfig at
 load time. The crypto.yaml file must be kept secret.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description: Shared root CA across all clusters (cert + private key).

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: Cluster intermediate CA, signed by root_ca.

fields.name: node_tls
fields.description: Per-node TLS server certificates (one per kernel/sentinel replica).

fields.name: node_signing_ca
fields.description: Per-node signing CAs for token issuance (one per kernel replica).

fields.name: edge_tls
fields.description:
Edge TLS certificates for gateway and oauth.
 Not used when tls.letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: edge_signing_ca
fields.description: Edge signing CAs.

fields.name: kmaker_signing_ca
fields.description:
Kmaker signing CA, signed by cluster_ca and constrained to issue only
 kernel bootstrap leaf certificates.

fields.name: optional_services
fields.description: Optional add-on services.

message.name: OptionalServices
message.description: OptionalServices controls which optional services are enabled.

fields.name: anthropic
fields.description: Proxy services — when enabled, one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description: MCP server — one replica when enabled.

fields.name: saml
fields.description:
SAML identity provider bridge — saml_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default.

fields.name: oauth
fields.description:
OAuth2/OIDC broker — oauth_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Enabled by default.

fields.name: keycloak
fields.description:
Keycloak IDP — production identity provider.
 Replaces mockidp. Enabled by default.

fields.name: output_dir
fields.description:
Filesystem path where generated Helm charts are written.
 Only used in GENERATE_ONLY mode. Default: "charts".

fields.name: web_root
fields.description:
Filesystem path to the web UI build, mounted read-only into gateway.
 Leave empty to use the gateway's embedded webapp.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
patch is the service image patch number to deploy.
 When 0 (default), the operator auto-tracks the latest patch and polls the
 registry for upgrades (every hour for stable, every 60s for dev builds).
 When set, the operator pins to that exact patch and does no polling.

fields.name: dev
fields.description:
dev selects dev builds when true, stable builds when false (default).
 Affects both the image tag suffix and the polling interval.

fields.name: gitlab_registry_token
fields.description:
gitlab_registry_token is an OAuth2 personal access token (read_registry scope)
 used to pull images from registry.gitlab.com. When set, the operator creates a
 "gitlab-registry" docker-registry Secret in the cavalier namespace as part of
 the generated Helm chart. Keep this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
SPIFFE trust-domain prefix for identity URIs. Every workload identity is
 formed as `spiffe://${spiffe_prefix}/${service_name}` — this powers token
 subject claims, mTLS URI SANs, and (post-B-end-state) SPIFFE-aware client
 cert verification. Operator propagates this value to kernel's bootstrap
 AND to every service configmap so all components agree on the trust
 domain at boot, without a runtime SCS round-trip.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, loaded from
 operator.yaml. The operator renders them into kernel's Helm-deployed config
 (kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs); kernel installs them into the root
 namespace's TenantConfig so they can provision tenants via TenantAdmin.
 Ordinary C2S CredPairs at the root namespace; only public halves are carried.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

fields.name: cluster_oauth
fields.description:
cluster_oauth holds shared (cluster-level) IDP providers — Google, GitHub, etc.
 Configured once by a cluster admin. Delivered to the oauth service for
 initial token validation; tenant routing happens via ClaimMatcher entries
 in each tenant's OAuthTenantConfig.

message.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
message.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:
ClusterOAuthProvider describes a shared IDP (e.g. Google, GitHub) available
 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. "https://accounts.google.com").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the shared OAuth app client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: kmaker
fields.description:
kmaker owns cluster bootstrap certificate signing for kernel. Operator
 renders this into kmaker's mounted runtime config and owns the Secret that
 carries kmaker.Config.signing_ca.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Cavalier cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.

 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

types.name: GetDescriptorRequest
types.description: GetDescriptorRequest asks for a named IDP's EntityDescriptor.

fields.name: idp_name
fields.description: idp_name matches the name field of an IdpConfig.

types.name: GetDescriptorResponse
types.description: GetDescriptorResponse returns the parsed IDP descriptor fields.

fields.name: entity_descriptor
fields.description: entity_descriptor is the parsed EntityDescriptor fields.

message.name: SamlEntityDescriptor
message.description:
SamlEntityDescriptor represents a SAML 2.0 EntityDescriptor metadata document.
 Used both to describe our own endpoints (SP or IDP role) and to parse external
 IDP metadata fetched during federation setup.

 Parallel to OIDC's /.well-known/openid-configuration discovery document.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: EntityId is the globally unique identifier for this SAML entity (a URI)

fields.name: signing_cert
fields.description:
SigningCert is the X.509 certificate whose private key signs assertions or
 AuthnRequests for this entity. Embedded as base64 DER in metadata XML.
 For IDP role: the key that signs assertions we issue.
 For SP role: the key that signs AuthnRequests we send (optional).

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: sso_services
fields.description:
SsoServices lists SingleSignOnService endpoints (IDP role only).
 External SPs use these URLs to send AuthnRequests.

message.name: SamlEndpoint
message.description:
SamlEndpoint describes a single SAML protocol endpoint with its binding and URL.
 Used in EntityDescriptor metadata to advertise service locations.

fields.name: binding
fields.description: Binding is the SamlBinding URI for this endpoint

fields.name: location
fields.description: Location is the endpoint URL

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Index is the endpoint index for indexed endpoints (e.g. AssertionConsumerService).
 Zero-valued for non-indexed endpoints such as SingleSignOnService.

fields.name: acs_urls
fields.description:
AcsUrls lists AssertionConsumerService endpoints (SP role only).
 IDPs POST SAMLResponses to these URLs.

fields.name: slo_services
fields.description: SloServices lists SingleLogoutService endpoints for both IDP and SP roles.

fields.name: want_authn_requests_signed
fields.description:
WantAuthnRequestsSigned indicates (IDP role) whether this IDP requires
 incoming AuthnRequests to be signed.

fields.name: authn_requests_signed
fields.description:
AuthnRequestsSigned indicates (SP role) whether this SP will sign its
 outgoing AuthnRequests.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this IDP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Okta", "Azure AD").

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the IDP's SAML entity ID (must match the Issuer element).

fields.name: metadata_url
fields.description:
metadata_url is the URL of the IDP's SAML EntityDescriptor XML.
 When set, the signing cert is fetched from this URL at startup.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: signing_cert_pem
fields.description:
signing_cert_pem is a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate used to verify
 assertion signatures from this IDP. If metadata_url is set, this is
 derived from the metadata. At least one of these must be provided.

fields.name: acs_path
fields.description:
acs_path is the relative path of our ACS endpoint for this IDP.
 Example: "/saml/acs/okta"
 Defaults to "/saml/acs" if empty.

fields.name: attribute_map
fields.description:
attribute_map maps IDP attribute names to Cavalier claim names.
 Keys are SAML attribute names (e.g. "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress").
 Values are the Cavalier claim names to pass to kernel (e.g. "email").
 If the "email" key is absent after mapping, the NameID is used as the subject.

fields.name: domains
fields.description: domains maps email domains to this IDP. Used for IDP selection hints.

types.name: ListSPsRequest
types.description: ListSPsRequest (empty — returns all enabled SPs).

types.name: ListSPsResponse
types.description: ListSPsResponse contains public SP information.

message.name: SpInfo
message.description: SpInfo is the public-facing information about a configured outbound SP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the display name.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the SP's SAML entity ID.

fields.name: sp_index
fields.description: sp_index identifies this SP in subsequent MintAssertion calls.

types.name: MapEmpty
MetadataRequest
types.description: MetadataRequest (empty — the service infers which entity descriptor to serve).

types.name: MetadataResponse
types.description: MetadataResponse contains the EntityDescriptor XML.

fields.name: xml
fields.description: xml is the EntityDescriptor XML document (UTF-8 encoded).

types.name: MintAssertionRequest
types.description: MintAssertionRequest asks SAML to issue a SAML assertion for a named SP.

fields.name: sp_index
fields.description: sp_index selects which configured SP to target.

fields.name: in_response_to
fields.description:
in_response_to is the ID of the SP's AuthnRequest, if SP-initiated.
 Empty for IDP-initiated flows.

types.name: MintAssertionResponse
types.description: MintAssertionResponse contains the issued SAML assertion.

fields.name: saml_response
fields.description:
saml_response is the base64-encoded signed <samlp:Response> XML.
 The caller should POST this to acs_url as the SAMLResponse form field.

fields.name: acs_url
fields.description: acs_url is the SP's AssertionConsumerService URL to POST to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: relay_state
fields.description:
relay_state is the relay_state to include in the POST (typically empty
 for IDP-initiated flows).

types.name: SamlAuthorizeRequest
types.description: SamlAuthorizeRequest initiates an SP-initiated SAML flow.

fields.name: idp_index
fields.description: idp_index selects which configured IDP to use.

fields.name: relay_state
fields.description: relay_state is the callback state to restore after authentication.

types.name: SamlAuthorizeResponse
types.description: SamlAuthorizeResponse contains the IDP redirect URL.

fields.name: redirect_url
fields.description: redirect_url is the full IDP SSO URL with embedded AuthnRequest.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description:
entity_id is the globally unique URI that identifies this SAML entity.
 It appears in the EntityDescriptor and in every assertion we issue.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com/saml"
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: base_url
fields.description:
base_url is the public HTTPS base URL of this service.
 Used to construct ACS, SSO, SLO, and metadata endpoint URLs.
 Example: "https://saml.example.com"
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

message.description: IdpConfig configures a single external IDP for inbound SAML flows (SP role).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this IDP.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Okta", "Azure AD").

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: entity_id is the IDP's SAML entity ID (must match the Issuer element).

fields.name: metadata_url
fields.description:
metadata_url is the URL of the IDP's SAML EntityDescriptor XML.
 When set, the signing cert is fetched from this URL at startup.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: signing_cert_pem
fields.description:
signing_cert_pem is a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate used to verify
 assertion signatures from this IDP. If metadata_url is set, this is
 derived from the metadata. At least one of these must be provided.

fields.name: acs_path
fields.description:
acs_path is the relative path of our ACS endpoint for this IDP.
 Example: "/saml/acs/okta"
 Defaults to "/saml/acs" if empty.

fields.name: attribute_map
fields.description:
attribute_map maps IDP attribute names to Cavalier claim names.
 Keys are SAML attribute names (e.g. "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress").
 Values are the Cavalier claim names to pass to kernel (e.g. "email").
 If the "email" key is absent after mapping, the NameID is used as the subject.

fields.name: domains
fields.description: domains maps email domains to this IDP. Used for IDP selection hints.

fields.name: sp_providers
fields.description: sp_providers is the list of external SP configurations for outbound flows.

rpcs.description:
MintAcsTokens accepts an inbound SAML assertion from an external IDP,
 verifies it, and mints Cavalier tokens.
 This is the POST endpoint that external IDPs redirect users to.
 The SAMLResponse form field contains the base64-encoded signed XML.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

rpcs.description:
Authorize initiates a SAML SP-initiated flow by building an AuthnRequest
 and returning the IDP redirect URL.
rpcs.verb_definition: Make an authorization decision (no state change).
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Authenticate/Guard; identity/entitlement decision only.

rpcs.description:
MintAssertion accepts a valid Cavalier JWT and produces a signed SAML
 assertion addressed to the named SP. The caller redirects the user to
 the SP's ACS URL with this assertion as the SAMLResponse POST body.

 This is the SAML parallel to ProxyTokenExchange.EnrichForProxy.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Create; credential/claim issuance, not durable resource creation.

types.name: Event
types.description:
Event is the top-level envelope for all typed events. It carries common
 context (source, identity, request tracing) and a typed payload.

 This is what gets published to EventBus, spooled for guaranteed delivery,
 and indexed by consumers.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the event timestamp in milliseconds since epoch (UTC).

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process.
 Format: "{service_id}-{instance_id}" for services (e.g., "identity-a1b2c3")
 or "{tool}-{user}" for clients (e.g., "mycli-alice").

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the x-request-id that traces a request across gateway,
 backend services, and client tools. Set by gateway, forwarded as gRPC
 metadata, extracted by generated wrappers.

fields.name: identity
fields.description:
identity is the caller's identity — the claims from the verified token.
 Enables identity-scoped event access — users query only their own events.
 Keys are claim names (sub, aud, iss, etc.), values are claim values.

fields.name: level
fields.description:

 Included on the envelope for filtering without inspecting the payload.

message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
types.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.name: archive_count
fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.name: dir
fields.description:
dir is the base directory (on the service's own volume) for the
 active / building / temp / archive files.

fields.name: file_permission
fields.description: file_permission is the Unix permission for the data files (e.g. 0600).

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

enums.name: Compression
enums.description:
Compression selects at-rest compression for rolled/archived files and
 snapshot baselines. The live redo-log append tail is always uncompressed so
 line appends stay cheap.

enums.name: EntitlementLevel
enums.description:
EntitlementLevel is the data-entitlement decision for one MAY_* field. The rule
 is FAIL-CLOSED: absent an explicit decision (UNSPECIFIED = 0, the proto3
 default), the field gets its MOST-PROTECTIVE level — MAY_REDACT defaults to
 REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE defaults to ANONYMIZE. A grant in the caller's token
 loosens a field toward RAW; it can never loosen below a hard floor
 (DROP/PSEUDONYMIZE fields are caller-independent and always applied).

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: No decision recorded — the field gets its most-protective default.

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_ANONYMIZE
values.description:
Replace with a keyed HMAC surrogate. Valid only on string/bytes fields; on any
 other field the generated transform clamps ANONYMIZE up to REDACT.

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_REDACT
values.description: Clear the field to its zero value (a message field clears the whole subtree).

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_RAW
values.description:
Egress the field raw — the explicit loosening grant ("this caller is
 permitted to see the value"). Only ever set from a matching token data grant.

types.name: Error
types.description:
Error represents a structured error with status information.
 This message is designed to work as a Go error type and follows the Google RPC error model.
 The generated code will have an Error() string method added to implement the error interface.
 See https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors for more information.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
Code is the status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.
 In Go, use google.golang.org/grpc/codes.Code for the status code.

fields.name: message
fields.description:
Message is a developer-facing error message, which should be in English.
 Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the details field,
 or localized by the client.

fields.name: details
fields.description:
Details is a list of messages that carry the error details.
 There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.

types.name: Config
types.description:
Config is the single configuration type for all services.

 Bootstrap fields (endpoints, instance_id, private_key, trusted_cas) are loaded
 from YAML at boot and used to connect to the cluster.

 Runtime fields (ping_interval_ms, rebalance_interval_ms, listen_address,
 max_request_size, request_timeout_seconds, logger, shutdown_timeout_seconds)
 are delivered by the cluster via ServiceConfigState and can change at any time.

 TLS certificates are obtained automatically by the servicemanager via X509Mint
 after token exchange — they are not part of the config.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.description:
Cluster endpoints. Set in bootstrap file; can be updated at runtime
 via ServiceConfigState to add/remove endpoints dynamically.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port

constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id uniquely identifies this running instance/replica.
 Used for leader elections on boundaries with (spec.leader) = true.
 If empty, a random ID is generated at client creation time.

fields.name: private_key
fields.description:
private_key is used to mint throwaway bootstrap JWTs for the
 token exchange flow. The kid is in private_key.id;
 identity (subject/audience) comes from the delegate looked up
 by TokenExchanger using the matching kid.
 If absent, cloud-native authentication is attempted.
