message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: ping_interval_ms
fields.description:
ping_interval_ms controls how often each endpoint is pinged for latency measurement.
 Default: 5000 (5 seconds)

fields.name: rebalance_interval_ms
fields.description:
rebalance_interval_ms controls how often the active connection is re-evaluated
 based on latency. Default: 10000 (10 seconds)

fields.name: listen_address
fields.description: listen_address is the bind address for the gRPC server. Default port 8443.

fields.name: max_request_size
fields.description:
max_request_size is the maximum request size in bytes.
 Must be greater than 0. Default: 10MB (10485760 bytes)

fields.name: request_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
request_timeout_seconds is the timeout for client requests.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description:
logger configures the logger for the service.
 Controls log format (JSON/console), level, output paths, and more.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_concurrent_streams
fields.description:
max_concurrent_streams limits the number of concurrent gRPC streams per connection.
 Prevents resource exhaustion from clients opening unlimited streams.
 Default: 100. Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default (unlimited).

fields.name: max_send_msg_size
fields.description:
max_send_msg_size is the maximum response message size in bytes.
 Prevents the server from sending responses that could OOM clients.
 Default: 16MB (16777216 bytes). Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default.

fields.name: keepalive_min_time_seconds
fields.description:
keepalive_min_time_seconds is the minimum interval clients must wait between
 keepalive pings. Clients pinging more frequently are disconnected.
 Default: 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable enforcement.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the explicit list of CA certificates trusted for SPIFFE TLS
 verification when connecting to cluster endpoints. It must not be empty.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain).
 It must not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path.
 Service identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on health reports or X509 URI SANs.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this service instance's topology path under /system —
 opaque, tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed
 (e.g. "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the
 SPIFFE segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the
 operator/deployment from runtime config (where the service runs); it is
 not a token claim. May be empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: disk_persistence
fields.description:
disk_persistence is an init-time/bootstrap setting that enables
 ServiceManager-owned redo-log lifecycle for generated service_store stores.
 When present at ServiceManager creation, the generated ServiceManager opens
 the per-store redo logs, exposes those handles to service code, and owns
 scheduled compaction/roll. It is not hot-reloaded; when absent, typed
 diskstore helpers remain available but no managed roll loop is started.

message.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
message.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.name: owner

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

fields.name: anonymize_hmac_key
fields.description:
anonymize_hmac_key is the per-deployment data-entitlement ANONYMIZE secret:
 the keyed-HMAC key the generated service wrapper supplies to Sanitize<T> so
 a value pseudonymizes to the same surrogate at any depth, across services
 and restarts. Required only by services whose records carry
 ANONYMIZE-capable (spec.redact) fields — the generated pseudonymize
 primitives fail loud on an empty key.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the port for a separate PLAINTEXT gRPC listener that
 serves ONLY grpc.health.v1. k8s kubelet probes are plaintext-only and
 cannot speak TLS, so the main TLS port (listen_address) is invisible to
 them. This listener runs on a completely separate grpc.Server / tonic
 Server / NettyServerBuilder with no TLS, no auth interceptors, and no
 business services registered — isolation is the security argument.
 The health status reflects the same StatusSink-driven state as the TLS
 health endpoint: NOT_SERVING until bootstrap completes, then tracks
 handler health (UNHEALTHY → NOT_SERVING, recovery → SERVING).
 Default: 8444. Set to 0 to disable the plaintext health probe listener.

   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_concurrent_streams
fields.description:
max_concurrent_streams limits the number of concurrent gRPC streams per connection.
 Prevents resource exhaustion from clients opening unlimited streams.
 Default: 100. Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default (unlimited).

fields.name: max_send_msg_size
fields.description:
max_send_msg_size is the maximum response message size in bytes.
 Prevents the server from sending responses that could OOM clients.
 Default: 16MB (16777216 bytes). Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default.

fields.name: keepalive_min_time_seconds
fields.description:
keepalive_min_time_seconds is the minimum interval clients must wait between
 keepalive pings. Clients pinging more frequently are disconnected.
 Default: 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable enforcement.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the explicit list of CA certificates trusted for SPIFFE TLS
 verification when connecting to cluster endpoints. It must not be empty.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain).
 It must not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path.
 Service identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on health reports or X509 URI SANs.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this service instance's topology path under /system —
 opaque, tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed
 (e.g. "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the
 SPIFFE segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the
 operator/deployment from runtime config (where the service runs); it is
 not a token claim. May be empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: disk_persistence
fields.description:
disk_persistence is an init-time/bootstrap setting that enables
 ServiceManager-owned redo-log lifecycle for generated service_store stores.
 When present at ServiceManager creation, the generated ServiceManager opens
 the per-store redo logs, exposes those handles to service code, and owns
 scheduled compaction/roll. It is not hot-reloaded; when absent, typed
 diskstore helpers remain available but no managed roll loop is started.

message.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
message.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.name: archive_count
fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.description:
dir is the base directory (on the service's own volume) for the

fields.name: file_permission
fields.description: file_permission is the Unix permission for the data files (e.g. 0600).

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

fields.name: anonymize_hmac_key
fields.description:
anonymize_hmac_key is the per-deployment data-entitlement ANONYMIZE secret:
 the keyed-HMAC key the generated service wrapper supplies to Sanitize<T> so
 a value pseudonymizes to the same surrogate at any depth, across services
 and restarts. Required only by services whose records carry
 ANONYMIZE-capable (spec.redact) fields — the generated pseudonymize
 primitives fail loud on an empty key.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the port for a separate PLAINTEXT gRPC listener that
 serves ONLY grpc.health.v1. k8s kubelet probes are plaintext-only and
 cannot speak TLS, so the main TLS port (listen_address) is invisible to
 them. This listener runs on a completely separate grpc.Server / tonic
 Server / NettyServerBuilder with no TLS, no auth interceptors, and no
 business services registered — isolation is the security argument.
 The health status reflects the same StatusSink-driven state as the TLS
 health endpoint: NOT_SERVING until bootstrap completes, then tracks
 handler health (UNHEALTHY → NOT_SERVING, recovery → SERVING).
 Default: 8444. Set to 0 to disable the plaintext health probe listener.

types.name: HttpClientConfig
types.description:
HttpClientConfig represents configuration for an HTTP client.
 It provides settings for TLS verification, keep-alive behavior, certificates, and timeouts.
 This configuration is typically used to create HTTP clients for making outbound requests
 with specific security and performance requirements.

fields.name: disable_keep_alives
fields.description:
DisableKeepAlives, if true, disables HTTP keep-alives and will close the connection
 after each request. This can reduce server load but increases latency for repeated requests.
 Default is false (keep-alives enabled).

fields.name: root_certs
fields.description:
RootCerts is a list of X.509 certificates to use as root CAs for verifying server certificates.
 If empty, the system's default root CAs will be used.
 Use this to trust custom or internal certificate authorities.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.description:
ClientCert is an X.509 certificate chain with private key for client authentication.
 Use this when the server requires mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication.
 chain[0] is the leaf cert, key must be set for mTLS.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

fields.name: id

fields.name: timeout_seconds
fields.description:
TimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds for the entire HTTP request/response cycle.
 This includes connection time, request writing, server processing, and response reading.
 A value of 0 uses the generated client default of 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_idle_conns
fields.description:
MaxIdleConns controls the maximum number of idle (keep-alive) connections across all hosts.
 A value of 0 means no limit. Default is typically 100 if not specified.

fields.name: max_idle_conns_per_host
fields.description:
MaxIdleConnsPerHost controls the maximum number of idle (keep-alive) connections per host.
 A value of 0 means use the default (typically 2). Increase for high-throughput scenarios.

fields.name: idle_conn_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
IdleConnTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds an idle connection will remain
 in the connection pool before being closed. A value of 0 means no limit.

fields.name: tls_handshake_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
TlsHandshakeTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a TLS handshake.
 A value of 0 means no timeout. Recommended: 10 seconds.

fields.name: expect_continue_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
ExpectContinueTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a server's
 first response headers after fully writing the request headers if the request has
 "Expect: 100-continue" header. A value of 0 means no timeout.

fields.name: response_header_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
ResponseHeaderTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a server's
 response headers after fully writing the request (including body, if any).
 A value of 0 means no timeout.

fields.name: retry_config
fields.description:
RetryConfig configures retry behavior for HTTP requests.
 If not specified, default retry configuration will be used (3 retries, jittered exponential backoff).

message.name: RetryConfig
message.description:
RetryConfig configures retry behavior for HTTP requests with jittered exponential backoff.
 This configuration controls how failed requests are retried, including which errors
 and status codes trigger retries, and the backoff timing between attempts.

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description:
MaxRetries is the maximum number of retry attempts after the initial request.
 A value of 0 means no retries (only the initial request is made).
 Default: 3

fields.name: initial_backoff_ms
fields.description:
InitialBackoffMs is the initial backoff duration in milliseconds before the first retry.
 This value is multiplied by BackoffMultiplier for each subsequent retry.
 Default: 100ms

fields.name: max_backoff_ms
fields.description:
MaxBackoffMs is the maximum backoff duration in milliseconds.
 The backoff will never exceed this value, even after many retries.
 Default: 5000ms (5 seconds)

fields.name: backoff_multiplier
fields.description:
BackoffMultiplier is the multiplier applied to the backoff duration after each retry.
 For exponential backoff, use values like 2.0 (doubles each time).
 For linear backoff, use 1.0 (stays constant).
 Default: 2.0

fields.name: retryable_status_codes
fields.description:
RetryableStatusCodes are HTTP status codes that should trigger a retry.
 Common retryable codes: 429 (Too Many Requests), 500, 502, 503, 504.
 If empty, defaults to [429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
 Network errors (connection failures, timeouts) are always retried regardless of this setting.

types.name: LoggerConfig
types.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

SessionIndex is the identifier for the session at the IDP.
 Used in single logout to identify which session to terminate.

fields.name: attributes
fields.description:
Attributes contains the AttributeStatement entries.
 Keys are SAML attribute names (e.g. "email", "groups").
 Values are attribute values; multi-valued attributes are comma-delimited.
 Parallel to the custom claims map in Token.

fields.name: xml
fields.description:
Xml contains the complete signed <samlp:Response> XML document.
 This field is populated by Sign() and must not be set manually.
 Parallel to the base64 field in Token.

types.name: SamlEndpoint
types.description:
SamlEndpoint describes a single SAML protocol endpoint with its binding and URL.
 Used in EntityDescriptor metadata to advertise service locations.

fields.name: binding
fields.description: Binding is the SamlBinding URI for this endpoint

fields.name: location
fields.description: Location is the endpoint URL

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Index is the endpoint index for indexed endpoints (e.g. AssertionConsumerService).
 Zero-valued for non-indexed endpoints such as SingleSignOnService.

types.name: SamlEntityDescriptor
types.description:
SamlEntityDescriptor represents a SAML 2.0 EntityDescriptor metadata document.
 Used both to describe our own endpoints (SP or IDP role) and to parse external
 IDP metadata fetched during federation setup.

 Parallel to OIDC's /.well-known/openid-configuration discovery document.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.description: EntityId is the globally unique identifier for this SAML entity (a URI)

fields.name: signing_cert
fields.description:
SigningCert is the X.509 certificate whose private key signs assertions or
 AuthnRequests for this entity. Embedded as base64 DER in metadata XML.
 For IDP role: the key that signs assertions we issue.
 For SP role: the key that signs AuthnRequests we send (optional).

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: sso_services
fields.description:
SsoServices lists SingleSignOnService endpoints (IDP role only).
 External SPs use these URLs to send AuthnRequests.

message.name: SamlEndpoint
message.description:
SamlEndpoint describes a single SAML protocol endpoint with its binding and URL.
 Used in EntityDescriptor metadata to advertise service locations.

fields.name: binding
fields.description: Binding is the SamlBinding URI for this endpoint

fields.name: location
fields.description: Location is the endpoint URL

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Index is the endpoint index for indexed endpoints (e.g. AssertionConsumerService).
 Zero-valued for non-indexed endpoints such as SingleSignOnService.

fields.name: acs_urls
fields.description:
AcsUrls lists AssertionConsumerService endpoints (SP role only).
 IDPs POST SAMLResponses to these URLs.

fields.name: slo_services
fields.description: SloServices lists SingleLogoutService endpoints for both IDP and SP roles.

fields.name: want_authn_requests_signed
fields.description:
WantAuthnRequestsSigned indicates (IDP role) whether this IDP requires
 incoming AuthnRequests to be signed.

fields.name: authn_requests_signed
fields.description:
AuthnRequestsSigned indicates (SP role) whether this SP will sign its
 outgoing AuthnRequests.

enums.name: SamlNameIdFormat
enums.description: SamlNameIdFormat represents SAML 2.0 NameID format URIs

enums.name: SamlBinding
enums.description: SamlBinding represents SAML 2.0 binding URIs for endpoint communication

enums.name: SamlAuthnContext
enums.description:
SamlAuthnContext represents SAML 2.0 authentication context class reference URIs.
 These appear in the AuthnStatement and describe the mechanism used to authenticate
 the subject at the asserting party.

values.name: SAML_AUTHN_CONTEXT_PASSWORD
values.description: PasswordProtectedTransport — username/password over TLS (most common for web SSO)

values.name: SAML_AUTHN_CONTEXT_TLS_CLIENT
values.description: TLSClient — mutual TLS with client certificate

values.name: SAML_AUTHN_CONTEXT_X509
values.description: X509 — X.509 certificate authentication

values.name: SAML_AUTHN_CONTEXT_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: Unspecified — authentication mechanism not specified

enums.name: SamlStatusCode
enums.description:
SamlStatusCode represents SAML 2.0 top-level status code URIs.
 These appear in the Status element of a SAMLResponse.

values.name: SAML_STATUS_CODE_SUCCESS
values.description: Success — the request succeeded

values.name: SAML_STATUS_CODE_REQUESTER
values.description: Requester — the request could not be performed due to an error on the requester's part

values.name: SAML_STATUS_CODE_RESPONDER
values.description: Responder — the request could not be performed due to an error on the responder's part

values.name: SAML_STATUS_CODE_VERSION_MISMATCH
values.description: VersionMismatch — the responder does not support the SAML version in the request

types.name: SmbCertDelivery
types.description:
SmbCertDelivery carries the instance's signed member cert and the isolated
 per-SMB trust anchor it must use for its peers.

 INVARIANT (soundness): ca is the per-SMB CA certificate ONLY — never the
 true/global ROOT CA — and no private key (neither the CA's nor any other) ever
 appears here. member_chain carries no private key; the instance holds its own
 member private key locally and never transmits it.

 CA. No private key — the instance generated and holds its keypair locally.

fields.name: chain

rpcs.description:
ManageSmbCert: bidi cert lifecycle for one SMB service instance. Any
 authenticated service may open a stream — the SecurityInterceptor validates
 the bearer token before the handler runs, and the handler matches the
 token's location-agnostic service path (token.service_path(), derived from
 sub_type/sub — never a raw SPIFFE URI claim) to the smb_service named in the
 first Init message.

 spec.smb_authority implements the server side; SMB service instances open the
 stream via the generated seam.

types.name: EventAnnotation
types.description:
EventAnnotation marks a message as an EventBus event: tacplus generates a topic
 and a publish RPC for it. The producer surface is declared (not defaulted):
 set c2s to expose the publish RPC to external clients (via gateway), s2s to
 expose it to internal services. At least one must be present; an internal-only
 event sets only s2s and is never exposed externally. spec.record implies
 spec.event (a record is an event that is also stored + projectable).

fields.name: c2s
fields.description: c2s, when present, exposes the publish RPC to external clients (via gateway).

message.name: MethodC2SAnnotation
message.description:
MethodC2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single C2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_c2s service.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:
auth_disabled: no token required for this RPC.
 Used for public endpoints like OIDC discovery and JWKS.

fields.name: auth_any_user
fields.description:
auth_any_user: any authenticated user can call this RPC
 (no entitlement check). Used for user-facing endpoints where
 any valid token is sufficient (e.g., token exchange, event streams).

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
target_namespace_field names the request field whose string value carries
 the target namespace path (e.g. "/io/example/tenant"). When set, the C2S
 authorizer enforces the level-or-below rule: the caller's namespace (from
 the bearer token's `namespace` claim) must equal the target namespace or
 be a strict path-segment ancestor of it. The field must exist on the
 request message and be of type string.

 Use the proto field name (snake_case as declared), e.g. "tenant_namespace".
 Leave unset for RPCs whose target is implicit (e.g. List* methods that
 scope the response to the caller's subtree at the handler).

fields.name: s2s
fields.description: s2s, when present, exposes the publish RPC to internal services.

message.name: MethodS2SAnnotation
message.description:
MethodS2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single S2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_s2s service.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description: auth_services overrides the service-level default for this method.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:

types.name: GraphFieldOption

fields.name: mode
fields.description:
mode controls whether this field is a graph predicate, included as JSON,
 or omitted entirely (UNSPECIFIED / absent).

enum_values.name: GRAPH_MODE_INCLUDE
enum_values.description:
Field is stored as a JSON blob. Not queryable, but preserved
 for round-trip fidelity. Suitable for maps, collections, and nested data
 that doesn't need graph traversal or filtering.

enum_values.name: GRAPH_MODE_PREDICATE
enum_values.description:
Field becomes a graph predicate with an index. Scalar fields map to
 typed predicates (string, int, float, bool, datetime). Message fields
 become uid edges — the target message must also have (spec.graph)
 annotations and exactly one upsert field.
 NOT valid on repeated fields or maps — use INCLUDE for collections.

fields.name: index
fields.description:
index is required when mode is PREDICATE and the field is a scalar type.
 Ignored for uid edges (message fields) and INCLUDE mode.
 Values depend on the graph store type:
   string:   "exact", "hash", "term", "fulltext", "trigram"
   int/uint: "int"
   float:    "float"
   bool:     "bool"
   datetime: "hour", "day", "month", "year"

fields.name: upsert
fields.description:
upsert marks this field as the identity predicate for upsert mutations.
 Exactly one field per message must be marked upsert: true when the message
 is the target of a uid edge from another message.
 Only valid with mode: PREDICATE.

fields.name: reverse
fields.description:
reverse marks a uid edge predicate as reverse-traversable, enabling
 traversal from child to parent (e.g., given a NetworkInfo node, find all
 ServiceInstances that reference it).
 Only valid with mode: PREDICATE on message-type fields.

types.name: GraphProjection
types.description:
GraphProjection declares a graph node type extracted from an event message.
 tacplus generates the node message with graph annotations, projection_source
 mappings, and conditional extraction logic for oneof fields.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the graph type name (e.g. "Session", "Agent", "ToolUse").

fields.name: xid
fields.description:
xid is the source field path used as the external ID for upserts.
 Dot notation accesses oneof payloads (e.g. "tool_use.tool_use_id").

fields.name: field
fields.description: field is the list of fields to include in the generated graph node.

message.name: GraphProjectionField
message.description: GraphProjectionField maps a source event field to a graph node predicate.

fields.name: source

types.name: GraphStoreAnnotation
types.description:
GraphStoreAnnotation marks a service proto as a graph data store.
 The store receives its projection data by auto-subscribing to the EventBus
 topics that carry its projection sources; no mutation service is generated.

types.name: GraphTypeAnnotation
types.description:
GraphTypeAnnotation marks a proto message as a graph type for schema generation.
 Used to generate mutation handlers and graph store projections.

 Design decisions (D1, D2, D3 from the graph schema plan):

 D1: Annotations go on SOURCE messages (e.g. GraphEntity in aegis.proto),
 not on the consumer. The source messages are the authority on the data model.
 This follows the same pattern as service_state, topic, and subscribe —
 the annotation lives where the structure is defined.

 D2: Nested messages WITHOUT graph_type are serialized as JSON string
 predicates. Graph storage is for traversal (structural fields), not
 analytical queries on metadata. JSON storage avoids ~50 null predicates
 per entity, prevents schema churn, and allows incremental promotion.

 D3: xid_field controls the mutation strategy. When set, subscribe-gen
 generates a conditional upsert by external id (xid) — query by xid,
 then update-or-insert. When empty, subscribe-gen generates JSON insert (append-only).

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the graph type name (e.g. "Entity", "Edge").

fields.name: xid_field
fields.description:
xid_field is the proto field used as the external ID for upserts.
 When set, subscribe-gen generates upsert mutations keyed on this field.
 When empty, subscribe-gen generates insert-only JSON mutations.

fields.name: source
fields.description:
source is the fully-qualified event message this graph type is extracted from.
 When set, subscribe-gen generates field extraction code that maps fields
 from the source event to this graph type using (spec.projection_source) annotations.
 Example: "sensor.SensorEvent"

types.name: GrpcC2SClient
types.description:
GrpcC2SClient declares a client-facing service dependency.
 Used as a file-level option to declare which services this package calls.
 tacplus.yaml selects whether that dependency emits C2S, W2S, or both.
 Example: option (spec.grpc_c2s_client) = {service: "gateway.TokenMint"};

fields.name: service
fields.description: service is "package.ServiceName" (e.g. "gateway.TokenMint").

types.name: GrpcConfigAnnotation
types.description:
GrpcConfigAnnotation marks a message as a gRPC service's configuration.
 tacplus uses these to auto-generate a generated.Services message that aggregates all
 gRPC configs, plus per-service config state boundaries.

fields.name: service_name
fields.description: service_name is the gRPC service name.

types.name: GrpcS2SClient
types.description:
GrpcS2SClient declares a service-to-service gRPC client dependency.
 Used as a file-level option to declare which S2S gRPC services this service calls.
 Proto package names are globally unique, so no file path is needed.
 tacplus resolves the package name to its proto file at build time.
 Example: option (spec.grpc_s2s_client) = {service: "identity.Mint"};

fields.name: service
fields.description: service is "package.ServiceName" (e.g. "identity.Mint").

types.name: GrpcW2SClient
types.description:
GrpcW2SClient declares a client-facing service dependency.
 Used as a file-level option to declare which services this package calls.
 tacplus.yaml selects whether that dependency emits C2S, W2S, or both.
 Example: option (spec.grpc_w2s_client) = {service: "dashboard.Dashboard"};

fields.name: service
fields.description: service is "package.ServiceName" (e.g. "dashboard.Dashboard").

types.name: IdentitySpiffeResource

fields.name: namespace_field
fields.description: namespace_field is the sibling field holding the namespace path.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: kind is the resource kind segment (a constant, validated as a single segment).

fields.name: id_field
fields.description: id_field is the sibling field holding the resource id.

types.name: IntConst
types.description:
File-level int constants.
 IntConst defines a named integer constant that can be used in file-level options.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the identifier for the constant

fields.name: value
fields.description: Value is the integer value of the constant

types.name: MethodC2SAnnotation
types.description:
MethodC2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single C2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_c2s service.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:
auth_disabled: no token required for this RPC.
 Used for public endpoints like OIDC discovery and JWKS.

fields.name: auth_any_user
fields.description:
auth_any_user: any authenticated user can call this RPC
 (no entitlement check). Used for user-facing endpoints where
 any valid token is sufficient (e.g., token exchange, event streams).

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
target_namespace_field names the request field whose string value carries
 the target namespace path (e.g. "/io/example/tenant"). When set, the C2S
 authorizer enforces the level-or-below rule: the caller's namespace (from
 the bearer token's `namespace` claim) must equal the target namespace or
 be a strict path-segment ancestor of it. The field must exist on the
 request message and be of type string.

 Use the proto field name (snake_case as declared), e.g. "tenant_namespace".
 Leave unset for RPCs whose target is implicit (e.g. List* methods that
 scope the response to the caller's subtree at the handler).

types.name: MethodCollection
types.description:
MethodCollection marks an RPC as a collection-returning read and declares its
 shape. The author declares intent plus a bound; tacplus derives transport,
 tiering, flow control, and lifecycle. See docs/API.md for the full model.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is required: SNAPSHOT (finite) or WATCH (open-ended).

enum_values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_SNAPSHOT
enum_values.description:
SNAPSHOT: a finite point-in-time set that terminates. Requires max_items.
 tacplus derives the delivery tier (inline / accumulated-stream / cursor)
 from max_items and the response's max element size.

enum_values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_WATCH
enum_values.description:
WATCH: an open-ended, change-driven stream (snapshot-then-deltas). Forbids
 max_items; uses a bounded replay ring (replay_depth) for resume.

enum_values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_PAGE
enum_values.description:
PAGE: a client-driven, resumable, windowed GET (unary). The caller pages
 through a finite set with an opaque keyset page_token over order_by; each
 page is bounded by page_size (capped at the trust-tier ceiling). Forbids
 max_items/replay_depth. See archive/RPC_PATTERNS_AND_VERBS_PLAN.md §4.

fields.name: order_by
fields.description:
order_by names the response fields that define a stable total order.
 Required for both modes (pagination cursors and the snapshot/delta boundary
 are only coherent over a stable order). tacplus appends a unique tiebreaker
 if these are not already total.

fields.name: max_items
fields.description:
max_items is the required, positive, finite item cap for SNAPSHOT reads.
 It is the routing key: tacplus computes max_items * max_item_bytes to pick
 the delivery tier. Forbidden on WATCH. Zero/unset on SNAPSHOT is an error.

fields.name: replay_depth
fields.description:
replay_depth is the WATCH replay-ring depth (count of retained changes).
 Optional; defaults to a platform constant. Forbidden on SNAPSHOT.

fields.name: default_page_size
fields.description:
default_page_size is the PAGE per-page window used when the request omits
 page_size. Required positive on PAGE; must be <= the trust-tier ceiling.
 Forbidden on SNAPSHOT/WATCH. PAGE only.

types.name: MethodS2SAnnotation
types.description:
MethodS2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single S2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_s2s service.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description: auth_services overrides the service-level default for this method.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:
auth_disabled: this RPC handles its own authentication internally.
 The caller interceptor skips this RPC entirely. Used for bootstrap
 bootstrap token-minting RPCs where callers authenticate via
 credentials in the request body (cred pair JWT), not via bearer token.

types.name: NumericConstraint
types.description:
NumericConstraint defines constraints for integer fields (int32, int64, uint32, uint64)
 This message supports complex validation scenarios beyond simple comparisons

fields.name: gt
fields.description: gt: field must be greater than this value

fields.name: ge
fields.description: ge: field must be greater than or equal to this value

fields.name: lt
fields.description: lt: field must be less than this value

fields.name: le
fields.description: le: field must be less than or equal to this value

fields.name: eq
fields.description: eq: field must equal this value

fields.name: ne
fields.description: ne: field must not equal this value

fields.name: in
fields.description: in: field must be one of these values

fields.name: not_in
fields.description: not_in: field must not be one of these values

fields.name: multiple_of
fields.description: multiple_of: field must be divisible by this value (field % multiple_of == 0)

types.name: OpaEvalAnnotation

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point is the OPA policy path (e.g. "data.entitlements.profiles").

fields.name: result
fields.description: result is the name of the result message in the same proto file.

types.name: OpaImport
types.description:
OpaImport declares a dependency on an OPA eval definition.
 Used as a file-level option so each proto package can declare which OPA
 evaluations it needs. tacplus generates a typed OpaEval client targeting
 the named physical service.
 Example:
   option (spec.opa_import) = {source: "userentitlements.EntitlementEvalInput", service: "opa"};

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is "package.InputMessageName" (e.g. "userentitlements.EntitlementEvalInput").

fields.name: service
fields.description:
service is the physical service that implements the OpaEval virtual service.
 Required. Build fails if the target does not import sys/opalib.proto.

types.name: ParamMapConfig
types.description:
ParamMapConfig configures automatic generation of FromMap methods
 This generates a method that converts a map[string]string to the message type,
 where the map keys correspond to enum values with json_return_value annotations

fields.name: key_enum
fields.description:
The enum type to use for parameter keys (e.g., "TokenParamKey")
 The enum must have json_return_value annotations on its values

fields.name: strict
fields.description: Whether to return an error on unknown keys (default: false, ignore unknown)

fields.name: validate_required
fields.description: Whether to return an error if required fields are missing (default: true)

types.name: QueryFieldOption
types.description: QueryFieldOption configures a record field as a RecordMap query filter criterion.

types.name: RecordAnnotation
types.description:
RecordAnnotation marks a message as a stored record: an event held in full by
 the record_store (stratum) and projectable to graph/timeseries stores. A record
 IS an event (it flows through eventbus); every record declares a key field
 (unique identifier) and an owner field (ownership/identity).

fields.name: key
fields.description: key is the proto field name used as the unique record identifier.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner is the proto field name that identifies the record's owner (e.g. spiffe_id).

fields.name: c2s
fields.description:
c2s, when present, exposes the record's publish RPC to external clients (via
 gateway). A record IS an event; this declares its producer surface the same
 way spec.event does. See EventAnnotation.

message.name: MethodC2SAnnotation
message.description:
MethodC2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single C2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_c2s service.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:
auth_disabled: no token required for this RPC.
 Used for public endpoints like OIDC discovery and JWKS.

fields.name: auth_any_user
fields.description:
auth_any_user: any authenticated user can call this RPC
 (no entitlement check). Used for user-facing endpoints where
 any valid token is sufficient (e.g., token exchange, event streams).

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
target_namespace_field names the request field whose string value carries
 the target namespace path (e.g. "/io/example/tenant"). When set, the C2S
 authorizer enforces the level-or-below rule: the caller's namespace (from
 the bearer token's `namespace` claim) must equal the target namespace or
 be a strict path-segment ancestor of it. The field must exist on the
 request message and be of type string.

 Use the proto field name (snake_case as declared), e.g. "tenant_namespace".
 Leave unset for RPCs whose target is implicit (e.g. List* methods that
 scope the response to the caller's subtree at the handler).

fields.name: s2s
fields.description: s2s, when present, exposes the record's publish RPC to internal services.

message.name: MethodS2SAnnotation
message.description:
MethodS2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single S2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_s2s service.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description: auth_services overrides the service-level default for this method.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:
auth_disabled: this RPC handles its own authentication internally.
 The caller interceptor skips this RPC entirely. Used for bootstrap
 bootstrap token-minting RPCs where callers authenticate via
 credentials in the request body (cred pair JWT), not via bearer token.

types.name: RecordStoreAnnotation
types.description:
RecordStoreAnnotation marks a service proto as the full-record store (stratum).
 Services with this annotation auto-subscribe to EventBus topics that publish
 the record types they store (currently spec.record). Hot/cold tiering is
 internal to the service.

types.name: RedactOption
types.description:
RedactOption configures a field (or, at message level via (spec.data_entitlement),
 a whole message default) with a data-entitlement mode.

types.name: RestMethods
types.description: RestMethods is a wrapper for repeated RestMethod, used in method options.

types.name: RetentionPolicy
types.description:
RetentionPolicy is a store-neutral statement of how long rows are retained.
 A downstream materializer renders this into an engine-specific TTL/eviction
 rule; tacplus carries only the semantic intent (which field, how long).

types.name: ServiceAnnotation
types.description: ServiceAnnotation declares the owning service identity for a proto file.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the canonical service name (e.g. "identity", "gateway").

fields.name: store
fields.description:
store declares this service as a backing store.
 Other services reference it via StateAnnotation.tag.

fields.name: gateway
fields.description:
gateway declares this service as a gateway (reverse proxy).
 Changes TLS source to GatewayTlsState (public cert) instead of X509Mint (internal CA).
 The generated run() watches GatewayTlsState for cert hot-reload instead of running
 a TLS renewal loop.

fields.name: rest_dispatch
fields.description:
rest_dispatch generates REST→gRPC dispatch code for all C2S RPCs visible
 to this service. The service acts as a reverse proxy, translating HTTP/JSON
 requests into typed gRPC calls. Used by gateway and the CLI.

types.name: ServiceC2DAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceC2DAnnotation declares a client-to-daemon gRPC service.
 Served over local IPC between CLI processes and a daemon.
 No auth required — filesystem permissions are the security boundary.

fields.name: socket_path
fields.description:
All c2d services are unauthenticated and localhost-only.

 socket_path is the Unix domain socket the daemon binds and clients dial.
 Required — there is no default. A shared default path would collide between
 daemons on the same host, so every c2d service declares its own path.

types.name: ServiceC2SAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceC2SAnnotation declares a client-to-service gRPC service.
 Exposed through the gateway to end users.
 Auth overrides (auth_disabled, auth_any_user) are method-level only —
 use spec.method_c2s on individual RPCs to override the default policy.
 Default policy: entitled users (gateway enforces entitlements).

fields.name: auth_entitled_users
fields.description:
auth_entitled_users: users with matching entitlements can call.
 This is the default C2S policy; set explicitly when entitlement
 checks are required for all RPCs in this service.

types.name: ServiceEventAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceEventAnnotation declares that a state service's topic/queue RPCs
 are accessible to other services (S2S only, like service_state).

fields.name: tag
fields.description: tag is the routing label for service resolution (e.g. "eventbus").

fields.name: export
fields.description: export makes this event topic available for RO import by other services.

types.name: ServiceHealthAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceHealthAnnotation declares a typed health message for a service.
 The annotated message MUST embed healthreport.ServiceInstanceHealth as field 1
 ("base"). The state store extracts .base for the generic health view and stores the
 full typed message per service (keyed by instance_id).
 Each node reports its own perspective of cluster health — Sentinel monitors
 consistency across perspectives and raises alarms on divergence.

types.name: ServiceS2SAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceS2SAnnotation declares a service-to-service gRPC service.
 Only authenticated service identities can call these RPCs.
 Auth overrides (auth_disabled) are method-level only — use spec.method_s2s
 on individual RPCs to disable auth for corner cases like bootstrap.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description:
auth_services: service identities allowed to call (service-level default).
 ["*"] = any service. Named entries restrict to those identities.
 Can be overridden per-method via spec.method_s2s.

fields.name: tag
fields.description:
tag is the routing label for the physical service that hosts this S2S
 interface. Used for vservice routing tables where the interface is defined
 in a vservice proto but hosted by a physical service (e.g. "stratum").

types.name: ServiceStoreAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceStoreAnnotation marks a message as a durable key-value store.
 Unlike service_state (convergent, fan-out, Watch), service_store is:
   - Write-with-quorum (writes acked only after replication to 2+ nodes)
   - Read-on-demand (no Watch streams, no client-side caching)
   - No boundary decomposition (the message IS the value)
 The store_key field annotation marks which field is the entry key.
 Access is via delegate pattern: services authenticate clients, then
 write through the backing service. External clients never write directly.

fields.name: tag
fields.description: tag is the routing label for the backing store (e.g. "state-store").

types.name: SmbAnnotation
types.description:
SmbAnnotation marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service and selects its trust root.
 The default root is SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

types.name: SmbAuthorityAnnotation
types.description:
SmbAuthorityAnnotation marks the consumer service that issues per-SMB CAs and
 member certs for spec.smb services (SPIFFE plan D7), declared
 EXPLICITLY rather than inferred. tacplus resolves the fully-qualified
 package.Service carrying this annotation as the SMB cert authority and fails
 generation if any spec.smb service exists with no authority declared. tacplus
 generates the authority contract and the SMB service's client seam; the
 designated consumer service implements the server side (CA keypair custody,
 member-cert signing, rotation). Exactly one authority should be annotated.
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "SmbAuthorityAnnotation",
  "package": "spec",
  "description": "SmbAuthorityAnnotation marks the consumer service that issues per-SMB CAs and
 member certs for spec.smb services (SPIFFE plan D7), declared
 EXPLICITLY rather than inferred. tacplus resolves the fully-qualified
 package.Service carrying this annotation as the SMB cert authority and fails
 generation if any spec.smb service exists with no authority declared. tacplus
 generates the authority contract and the SMB service's client seam; the
 designated consumer service implements the server side (CA keypair custody,
 member-cert signing, rotation). Exactly one authority should be annotated.",
  "fields": []
}

types.name: StateAnnotation
types.description: StateAnnotation marks a message as a state root and references its backing store.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the state root name (e.g. "ClusterState", "AegisState").

fields.name: tag
fields.description: tag is the routing label for the backing store (e.g. "state-store", "eventbus").

fields.name: auto_tls
fields.description:
auto_tls enables automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 When set, tacplus generates a bidi stream subscription to the certificate
 authority service and a new_tls_cert Handler method for cert delivery.
 The service generates keypairs locally; the certificate authority signs and
 delivers certs, triggering renewal at half-life.

enum_values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE
enum_values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE disables auto-TLS (default).

enum_values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519
enum_values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519 uses Ed25519 (OKP) keys.

enum_values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA
enum_values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA uses ECDSA P-256 keys.

fields.name: export
fields.description:
export makes this state root available for RO import by other services.
 Without export, the state is private to the owning service.

types.name: StateImport
types.description:
StateImport is the legacy file-level mirror for field-level state_import
 declarations. The target state must have export=true on its service_state.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is "package.StateName" (e.g. "identity.Identity", "aegis.AegisState").

types.name: StringConst
types.description:
File-level string constants.
 StringConst defines a named string constant that can be used in file-level options.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the identifier for the constant

fields.name: value
fields.description: Value is the string value of the constant

types.name: SubscriptionAnnotation
types.description:
SubscriptionAnnotation declares that this state service subscribes to
 an event-bus topic from another service's state root.

fields.name: source
fields.description:
source is the fully-qualified topic reference: "package.StateRoot.field_name"
 e.g., "claudesensor.AgenticCodeEventBus.event_stream"

types.name: TimeseriesFieldOption

fields.name: order_key
fields.description: Position in the store-neutral sort-key role (1-indexed). 0 = not a sort key.

fields.name: partition_key
fields.description: Part of the store-neutral partition role.

fields.name: cardinality_hint
fields.description: Store-neutral hint about the column's distinct-value count.

types.name: TimeseriesProjection
types.description:
TimeseriesProjection declares a timeseries table type extracted from an event.
 tacplus generates the record message with timeseries_column annotations and
 projection_source mappings. Common context fields from the source event are
 included automatically — only payload-specific fields need listing. The shape
 is store-neutral: retention and dedup are declared as semantic intent, and a
 downstream materializer renders the concrete engine/TTL/merge behavior.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the table/record type name (e.g. "SessionRecord").

fields.name: when
fields.description:
when is the oneof variant name that triggers this record (e.g. "session").
 Only events carrying this payload variant produce a row.

fields.name: field
fields.description: field lists payload-specific fields beyond the common context.

message.name: TimeseriesProjectionField
message.description: TimeseriesProjectionField maps a source event field to a timeseries column.

fields.description: source is the field path on the source event (e.g. "session.model").

fields.name: as
fields.description: as renames the column in the generated record (defaults to last segment of source).

fields.name: order_key
fields.description:
order_key is the column's position in the store-neutral sort-key role
 (0 = not a sort key). A materializer maps this to the engine's sort order.

fields.name: partition_key
fields.description: partition_key marks this column as part of the store-neutral partition role.

fields.name: cardinality_hint
fields.description: cardinality_hint is a store-neutral hint about the column's distinct-value count.

fields.name: retention
fields.description: retention is the store-neutral row retention policy (unset = indefinite).

message.name: RetentionPolicy
message.description:
RetentionPolicy is a store-neutral statement of how long rows are retained.
 A downstream materializer renders this into an engine-specific TTL/eviction
 rule; tacplus carries only the semantic intent (which field, how long).

fields.name: dedup
fields.description: dedup is the store-neutral duplicate-resolution policy.

message.name: DedupPolicy
message.description:
DedupPolicy is a store-neutral statement of row identity and duplicate
 resolution. A downstream materializer maps this onto an engine's merge/dedup
 mechanism; tacplus carries only the semantic intent.

types.description: TimeseriesProjectionField maps a source event field to a timeseries column.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is the field path on the source event (e.g. "session.model").

fields.name: as
fields.description: as renames the column in the generated record (defaults to last segment of source).

fields.name: order_key
fields.description:
order_key is the column's position in the store-neutral sort-key role
 (0 = not a sort key). A materializer maps this to the engine's sort order.

fields.name: partition_key
fields.description: partition_key marks this column as part of the store-neutral partition role.

fields.name: cardinality_hint

types.description:
TimeseriesStoreAnnotation marks a service proto as a timeseries data store.
 The store receives its projection data by auto-subscribing to the EventBus
 topics that carry its projection sources; no mutation service is generated.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Table name. Default: snake_case of message name.

fields.name: source

Source event FQN for field extraction.

 from the source event to this projection.
 Example: "sensor.SensorEvent"

 A downstream materializer renders this into an engine-specific TTL/eviction
 rule; tacplus carries only the semantic intent (which field, how long).
