TokenMinterAnnotation marks a service as the cluster's token minter, declared
 EXPLICITLY rather than inferred from RPC signatures. The bootstrap token
 exchanger (service_im / client_im codegen) targets the service carrying this
 annotation, resolving its fully-qualified package.Service. Exactly one
 authoritative minter should be annotated.

fields.name: proxy
fields.description:
proxy marks the client-reachable C2S front (e.g. gateway.Mint) that proxies
 to the authoritative S2S minter. Clients with no S2S identity mint through
 this proxy; services with an S2S identity call the authoritative minter
 (proxy = false) directly.

types.name: VServiceAnnotation
types.description:
VServiceAnnotation declares a virtual service identity for a proto file.
 Virtual services have their RPCs hosted by a physical service (e.g., eventbus)
 but are authorized separately. The id is a stable field number for TokenEntitlements
 (use range 30+ to avoid collision with physical service IDs).

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the canonical vservice name used as the entitlement key (e.g., "claudesensor").

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is the stable field number in TokenEntitlements for this vservice.

enums.name: IpAddrTypes
enums.description:
IpAddrTypes defines validation types for IP addresses, masks, and networks.
 Used in field options to enforce IP address format validation.

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED represents an unspecified IP address type

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V4
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V4 validates IPv4 addresses (e.g., 1.1.1.1)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V6
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V6 validates IPv6 addresses (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_ANY
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_ANY validates either IPv4 or IPv6 addresses

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V4
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V4 validates IPv4 subnet masks (e.g., 0-32)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V6
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V6 validates IPv6 subnet masks (e.g., 0-128)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_ANY
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_ANY validates either IPv4 or IPv6 subnet masks

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V4
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V4 validates IPv4 CIDR networks (e.g., 1.1.1.1/32)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V6
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V6 validates IPv6 CIDR networks (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3::8a2e:0370:7334/128)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_ANY
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_ANY validates either IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR networks

enums.name: EncType
enums.description:
EncType defines validation types for cryptographic keys and certificates.
 Used in field options to enforce key format and algorithm validation.

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_UNDEFINED
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_UNDEFINED represents an unspecified encryption key type

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_RSA validates private RSA keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_RSA validates public RSA keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_RSA validates either private or public RSA keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_EC validates private Elliptic Curve keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_EC validates public Elliptic Curve keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_EC validates either private or public EC keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ED25519 validates private Ed25519 keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ED25519 validates public Ed25519 keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_ED25519 validates either private or public Ed25519 keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ANY validates private keys of any algorithm (RSA, EC, Ed25519)

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ANY validates public keys of any algorithm

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY validates any key (private or public) of any algorithm

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_RSA validates X.509 certificates with RSA public keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_EC validates X.509 certificates with EC public keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ED25519 validates X.509 certificates with Ed25519 public keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ANY validates X.509 certificates with any key algorithm

enums.name: SqlPermit
enums.description:
SqlPermit defines validation types for SQL statement fields.
 Used in field options to enforce a syntactic sanity check plus a statement-type restriction.
 This is NOT an injection defense: the validator only rejects a handful of obvious tokens
 (semicolons, -- and /* comments, backslash escapes) and checks the leading keyword. A
 syntactically valid statement can still carry an injection payload (e.g. a UNION or a
 subquery in a permitted SELECT), and the check does not cover all comment syntaxes (e.g.
 '#' line comments). Callers MUST use parameterized queries and MUST NOT interpolate a validated
 string into a query as though it were safe.

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_UNSPECIFIED represents an unspecified SQL permit type

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_SELECT
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_SELECT allows only SELECT statements (including WITH ... SELECT CTEs)

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_DML
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_DML allows SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE statements

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_DDL
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_DDL allows CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE statements

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_ANY
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_ANY applies only the syntactic sanity check, with no statement-type restriction

enums.name: Azp
enums.description:
Azp enumerates the authorized-party / attestation contexts a kernel-minted
 token may record (SPIFFE plan D4). It is the proto-defined source of truth for
 the `azp` claim — generated code carries no hardcoded azp list. `azp` is the
 attestation path, NOT part of the subject identity, and kernel sets it from
 trusted context (never copied from untrusted request claims).

values.name: AZP_KERNEL
values.description: kernel: minted by kernel from trusted internal context (service/bootstrap).

values.name: AZP_OAUTH
values.description:
oauth: user attested via an OAuth broker; kernel maps the broker's
 authenticated S2S identity to this value at MintUserToken.

values.name: AZP_SAML
values.description: saml: user attested via a SAML broker; mapped by kernel as for oauth.

values.name: AZP_CLOUD_AUTH
values.description:
cloud-auth: reserved for the future cloud-auth attestation broker. No
 runtime mints this except tests until that broker exists (D4).

enums.name: TypeKind
enums.description: TypeKind classifies protobuf field kinds for generated registry metadata.

enums.name: CardinalityHint
enums.description:
CardinalityHint is a store-neutral hint about how many distinct values a
 column holds. A downstream materializer may use it to pick an encoding, but
 tacplus emits no concrete codec — the hint is pure semantic intent.

enums.name: DedupStrategy
enums.description: DedupStrategy is a store-neutral statement of how duplicate rows are resolved.

enums.name: GraphMode
enums.description:
GraphMode controls how a field is persisted in graph storage.
 UNSPECIFIED means the field is omitted (not stored).
 Annotations are opt-in: fields without (spec.graph) are not persisted.

values.name: GRAPH_MODE_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: Field is not stored in graph storage.

values.name: GRAPH_MODE_INCLUDE
values.description:
Field is stored as a JSON blob. Not queryable, but preserved
 for round-trip fidelity. Suitable for maps, collections, and nested data
 that doesn't need graph traversal or filtering.

values.name: GRAPH_MODE_PREDICATE
values.description:
Field becomes a graph predicate with an index. Scalar fields map to
 typed predicates (string, int, float, bool, datetime). Message fields
 become uid edges — the target message must also have (spec.graph)
 annotations and exactly one upsert field.
 NOT valid on repeated fields or maps — use INCLUDE for collections.

enums.name: SmbRoot
enums.description: SmbRoot selects which trust root backs an SMB service's member certificates.

values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

enums.name: CollectionMode
enums.description:
CollectionMode declares how a multi-result read behaves. See docs/API.md.
 A read returning more than one result must declare exactly one mode; an
 unbounded SNAPSHOT is a contradiction (if it is unbounded, it is a WATCH).

values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_SNAPSHOT
values.description:
SNAPSHOT: a finite point-in-time set that terminates. Requires max_items.
 tacplus derives the delivery tier (inline / accumulated-stream / cursor)
 from max_items and the response's max element size.

values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_WATCH
values.description:
WATCH: an open-ended, change-driven stream (snapshot-then-deltas). Forbids
 max_items; uses a bounded replay ring (replay_depth) for resume.

values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_PAGE
values.description:
PAGE: a client-driven, resumable, windowed GET (unary). The caller pages
 through a finite set with an opaque keyset page_token over order_by; each
 page is bounded by page_size (capped at the trust-tier ceiling). Forbids
 max_items/replay_depth. See archive/RPC_PATTERNS_AND_VERBS_PLAN.md §4.

enums.name: QueryOp
enums.description: QueryOp is the match kind for a (spec.query_field) record filter criterion.

enums.name: RedactMode
enums.description:
RedactMode selects the data-entitlement transform for a field on its way out
 of a service (egress-only, e.g. Sample/Pull). It expresses the four states of
 the data-entitlement lattice across two transform kinds (redact, anonymize)
 and two floors (hard "is-*", eligible "may-*"). Effective level per field is
 max(annotation floor, runtime entitlement) under pass-through < anonymize <
 redact — the runtime entitlement can only ratchet tighter, never loosen below
 the floor. The two "is-*" modes are the original unconditional behavior.

enums.name: EvictionPolicy
enums.description:
EvictionPolicy determines which entries to evict when max_size is reached.
 Used as a field-level annotation on boundary fields and as a message-level
 default on state root messages.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_NONE
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_NONE disables eviction (default). Entries are never evicted by policy.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_LRU
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_LRU evicts least recently used entries.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_LFU
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_LFU evicts least frequently used entries.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_RANDOM
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_RANDOM evicts entries randomly.

enums.name: MaxSizePolicy
enums.description: MaxSizePolicy determines what the eviction_max_size limit refers to.

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_ENTRY_COUNT
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_ENTRY_COUNT limits by total number of entries (default).

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_SIZE
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_SIZE limits by heap memory used in bytes.

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_PERCENTAGE
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_PERCENTAGE limits by percentage of heap memory used.

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_FREE_HEAP_PERCENTAGE
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_FREE_HEAP_PERCENTAGE evicts when free heap drops below percentage.

enums.name: TlsKeyType
enums.description: TlsKeyType specifies the key algorithm for auto-TLS certificate management.

values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE
values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE disables auto-TLS (default).

values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519
values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519 uses Ed25519 (OKP) keys.

values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA
values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA uses ECDSA P-256 keys.

enums.name: ConfigSliceScope
enums.description:
ConfigSliceScope identifies the aggregate config message that receives a
 per-service config slice.

enums.name: RestMethod
enums.description:
RestMethod enumerates additional HTTP methods for REST exposure.
 POST is always implicit on every convention REST route and does not
 appear in this enum. These values are used with spec.rest_method to
 declare additional HTTP methods for an RPC.

types.name: BoundaryInfo
types.description:
BoundaryInfo describes a state boundary in a tacplus build.
 This is language-neutral metadata exposed by generated registry code.

fields.name: service
fields.description:
Owning service, as the project-specific ServiceName enum. Like
 RpcInfo.service, this is a placeholder POPULATED DOWNSTREAM once the full
 ServiceName enum is generated into generated/services.proto — it is
 SERVICE_NAME_UNSPECIFIED in the base registry tacplus emits (the base enum has
 only UNSPECIFIED/ANY). For the owning-service identifier tacplus actually
 emits, use `tag` (field 15), the service_state routing tag.

fields.name: state_root
fields.description: State root message name, e.g. "ClusterState".

fields.name: boundary
fields.description: Boundary field name, e.g. "ClusterInfo".

fields.name: persistence
fields.description: True when the boundary is persisted.

fields.name: collection
fields.description: True when the boundary is a collection (repeated field).

fields.name: type_fqn
fields.description: Fully qualified type name of the boundary message.

fields.name: boundary_callers
fields.description: Cross-namespace callers allowed on this boundary field.

fields.name: rpcs
fields.description: RPCs that operate on this boundary (derived from naming convention).

fields.name: is_config
fields.description: True when this boundary is a configuration boundary (ConfigState pattern).

fields.name: tag
fields.description: Routing tag from service_state annotation (e.g., "state-store", "eventbus").

fields.name: graph_type
fields.description:
Graph type of this boundary: "singleton", "collection", "topic",
 "queue", "priority_queue", "command", "view", "state_import", "private".

fields.name: auto_tls_key_type
fields.description:
auto_tls_key_type is the key algorithm when auto_tls is enabled ("ed25519" or "ecdsa").
 Empty means auto_tls is disabled.

fields.name: collected_health
fields.description: True when this boundary is marked for Sentinel health collection.

types.name: BuildInfo
types.description: BuildInfo contains version and build metadata for the registry.

fields.name: tacplus_version
fields.description: tacplus version that generated this registry.

fields.name: build_timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp when the registry was generated (RFC 3339).

fields.name: source_git_sha
fields.description: Git SHA of the source proto directory, if available.

types.name: ClientDependencyInfo
types.description: ClientDependencyInfo describes a file-level declared gRPC client dependency.

fields.name: source_package
fields.description: source_package is the proto package that declares the dependency.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", or "w2s".

fields.name: service
fields.description: service is the declared target service ref, usually "package.ServiceName".

fields.name: target_package
fields.description: target_package is parsed from service when service is package-qualified.

fields.name: target_service
fields.description: target_service is parsed from service when service is package-qualified.

fields.name: wildcard
fields.description: wildcard is true for spec.all_grpc_s2s_clients.

types.name: DedupPolicyInfo
types.description:
DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral
 row identity + duplicate-resolution policy. A downstream materializer maps this
 onto an engine's merge/dedup mechanism.

fields.description:

 Always present for gateway-exposed RPCs: {REST_ROOT_PATH}/{package}/{Service}/{MethodName}.
 The service segment mirrors the gRPC + entitlement-grant identity so routes
 stay collision-free when a package hosts multiple services sharing a method.

fields.name: rpc_verb
fields.description:

enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER

fields.description: Full gRPC method path, e.g. "/policy.PolicyService/GetApiCatalog".

fields.name: http_path
fields.description:
HTTP REST convention path, e.g. "/api/v1/identity/IdentityService/ListProviders".
 Always present for gateway-exposed RPCs: {REST_ROOT_PATH}/{package}/{Service}/{MethodName}.
 The service segment mirrors the gRPC + entitlement-grant identity so routes
 stay collision-free when a package hosts multiple services sharing a method.

fields.name: http_methods
fields.description:
HTTP methods for REST access. POST is always present for convention routes.
 Additional methods come from spec.rest_method (e.g. ["POST", "GET"]).

fields.name: http_alias_path
fields.description:
HTTP alias path from spec.rest_path, relative to REST_ROOT_PATH.
 When present, creates an additional route (e.g. "/api/v1/.well-known/openid-configuration").
 Same http_methods apply to the alias.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description: Auth policy — inherited from service-level annotation.

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description:
auth_model: "s2s" (service-to-service), "c2s" (client-to-service),
 or "c2d" (client-to-daemon local IPC).

fields.name: collection_mode
fields.description:
method_collection (collection-returning read) — see docs/API.md.
 collection_mode is "SNAPSHOT" | "WATCH" | "PAGE"; empty when the RPC is not
 a collection read. The remaining fields are the declared bounds.

fields.name: collection_default_page_size
fields.description:
PAGE keyset default page size when the request omits a limit (0 on
 SNAPSHOT/WATCH). The wrapper bounds an explicit limit to collection_max_items.

fields.name: rpc_verb
fields.description:
Governed RPC classification derived from the method name and streaming /
 collection shape. Empty when the method does not yet classify cleanly.

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
Namespace authorization metadata. These fields expose the same level-or-below
 decision inputs that generated authorizers enforce at runtime.

fields.name: verb_status
fields.description: verb_status is "classified", "unclassified", or "exempt".

fields.name: folded_to_verb
fields.description: folded_to_verb is the canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.description:
surfaces lists every generated transport/auth surface for this RPC. This
 includes derived W2S gRPC-over-REST exposure when a C2S RPC has REST route
 metadata.

fields.name: smb
fields.description:
smb marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service: its own instances talk over a
 black-box peer protocol within a single cluster (SPIFFE
 plan D7). Consumers read this from the registry, not proto text, to drive
 the per-SMB CA + member-cert wiring.

fields.name: smb_authority
fields.description:
smb_authority marks the consumer service designated to issue per-SMB CAs +
 member certs for smb services (SPIFFE plan D7). Read from the registry so an
 SMB service / its tooling can resolve which service to obtain its CA + cert
 from. tacplus does not implement the authority.

fields.name: smb_root
fields.description:
smb_root is present when smb is true and records the trust profile selected
 by spec.smb. SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED is the default; SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER requests a
 per-SMB intermediate rooted in the cluster CA.

types.name: TagSelectorRequirement
TagSet
types.description: TagSet is a set of key/value tags. Keys are unique within the map.
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "TagSet",
  "package": "tags",
  "description": "TagSet is a set of key/value tags. Keys are unique within the map.",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "tags",
      "type": "map",
      "repeated": true,
      "constraints": [
        "maximum size: 1024 entries (default)",
        "maximum key size: 32768 bytes (default)",
        "maximum value size: 32768 bytes (default)"
      ],
      "constraint_infos": [
        {
          "rule": "default_max_size",
          "target": "field",
          "value_kind": "int",
          "int_value": 1024,
          "defaulted": true,
          "unit": "entries",
          "source": "default_bound"
        },
        {
          "rule": "default_max_key_size",
          "target": "key",
          "value_kind": "int",
          "int_value": 32768,
          "defaulted": true,
          "unit": "bytes",
          "source": "default_bound"
        },
        {
          "rule": "default_max_value_size",
          "target": "value",
          "value_kind": "int",
          "int_value": 32768,
          "defaulted": true,
          "unit": "bytes",
          "source": "default_bound"
        }
      ],
      "map_key_type": "string",
      "map_value_type": "string"
    }
  ]
}

rpcs.description:
ManageCert: bidi cert lifecycle. Any authenticated service may open a
 stream — the SecurityInterceptor validates the bearer token before
 the handler runs, and the handler matches the token's location-agnostic
 service path (token.service_path(), derived from sub_type/sub — never a
 raw SPIFFE URI claim) to the requested service_name in the first Init
 message.

services.name: TlsCertService
services.description:
TlsCertService provides automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 The certificate authority service implements the server side. Services with
 auto_tls: true open a bidi stream via the generated ServiceManager.

 Flow:
   1. Service sends Init (identifies itself) + Csr (public key)
   2. Certificate authority signs cert under service's intermediate CA, returns CertDelivery
   3. At half-life, certificate authority sends Renew
   4. Service generates new keypair, sends Csr
   5. Certificate authority signs, returns CertDelivery
   6. Repeat from 3

values.name: JWT_PAYLOAD_TYPE_NAMESPACE
values.description:
--- Namespace (authorization scope) ---
 `namespace` is the caller's authorization-tree scope, e.g. "/" (root),
 "/system/...", "/tenants/acme", or "/tenants/acme/workspaces/dev". It is
 an authorization fact, NOT the subject identity. The subject SPIFFE ID is
 a COMPUTATION over the structured claims (sub_type, sub, namespace,
 service_name) performed by the generated sys/spiffe helper
 (token.subject_spiffe_id); it is never carried as a wire claim. The
 universal level-or-below rule (target_namespace_field) compares namespace
 paths directly via the path-segment-aware is_at_or_below relation.

message.name: TraceRound
message.description: TraceRound identifies a single service hop in a traced request.

fields.name: rpc
fields.description:
rpc identifies the specific service and method being traced using the
 generated AccountingMethod enum type. Exactly one field is set to the
 corresponding RPC enum value; all others default to 0.

message.name: AccountingMethod
message.description:
AccountingMethod identifies which RPC an event relates to.
 Only one field will be set — the rest default to 0 (UNSPECIFIED)
 and are not encoded by proto3, so there is no overhead.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: kind classifies where in the request lifecycle this event was emitted.

fields.name: error
fields.description:
error is set on response events when the request failed (auth rejection,
 backend unavailable, handler error, etc.). Empty on success.

types.name: TraceRequest
types.description:
TraceRequest replaces google.protobuf.Empty on the gRPC wire for RPCs with
 empty input types. This ensures every RPC can be traced, even read-only
 endpoints that take no parameters. The handler interface stays arg-free —
 TraceRequest has no user-meaningful fields.

types.name: TraceRound
types.description: TraceRound identifies a single service hop in a traced request.

enums.name: TraceEventKind
enums.description:
TraceEvent is published per-hop to the trace topic when a traced message
 passes through a service. EventBus matches these to active WatchTrace streams
 by trace_id. Ordering is determined by timestamp_ms in TraceRound.
 TraceEventKind classifies the trace event within the request lifecycle.
 External events are emitted by the gateway (edge); internal events are
 emitted by backend services.

fields.name: sql

 Stratum resolves those event_ids against the event store.

types.name: EntitlementEvalInput
types.description:
EntitlementEvalInput is the input to the entitlements OPA policy.
 tacplus generates a typed EvalEntitlement RPC on opa from this message.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the IDP-provided identity claims (e.g. email, groups, roles).
 Uses google.protobuf.Struct to preserve native JSON types (arrays, objects, booleans).

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's project namespace (e.g. "/local/dev/drpepper").
 OPA dispatches on it to run that project's policy. Empty = cluster-root policy.

types.name: EntitlementEvalResult
types.description:
EntitlementEvalResult is the output of the entitlements OPA policy.
 The policy returns a TokenEntitlements directly — kernel embeds it in the
 JWT service_entitlements claim without any further expansion.

fields.name: token_entitlements
fields.description: token_entitlements holds the per-service RPC grants returned by OPA.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: all_entitlements
fields.description:
all_entitlements grants unrestricted access to all services and RPCs.
 When true, kernel sets service_entitlements={"all":true} in the JWT,
 and gateway bypasses per-service entitlement checks entirely.
 Intended for admin users only.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the tenant namespace the policy assigns to this caller, as a
 leading-slash absolute path (e.g. "/local/dev/acme"). IDP+OPA live at the
 tenant level, so this is the tenant subtree the caller's issuer/claims map
 to. When empty, kernel falls back to the cluster-root namespace.

fields.name: authorized_projects
fields.description:
authorized_projects are the project leaf names within the tenant that this
 caller may obtain an access token for (e.g. ["prod", "staging"]). The
 minted AT is always scoped to exactly one of these; a project switch
 re-mints against this list without requiring re-login. Leaf segments,
 relative to `namespace`.

fields.name: default_project
fields.description:
default_project is the project the caller is scoped to immediately after
 login, when no explicit project is requested. Must be one of
 authorized_projects. Leaf segment, relative to `namespace`.

rpcs.description: entry_point: data.entitlements.eval

services.name: OpaEval
services.description:
Generated by tacplus from spec.opa_eval annotations.
 tacplus:generated-service

rpcs.description: entry_point: data.entitlements.eval

types.name: ProxyPolicyEvalInput
types.description:
ProxyPolicyEvalInput is the input to the proxy policy OPA evaluation.
 tacplus generates a typed EvalProxyPolicy RPC on opa from this message.
 Kernel calls this before minting an external token — the caller's JWT payload
 and opaque routing metadata are the inputs the policy uses to decide.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the caller's JWT payload claims (e.g. sub, email, groups,
 service_entitlements). Uses google.protobuf.Struct to preserve native
 JSON types (arrays, objects, booleans).

fields.name: metadata
fields.description:
metadata is the opaque string from the cavalierctl listener config,
 forwarded verbatim by the proxy. The policy uses it to determine which
 upstream is being targeted (e.g. by mapping to a known URL or label)
 and whether the caller is permitted to reach it.

types.name: ProxyPolicyEvalResult
types.description:
ProxyPolicyEvalResult is the output of the proxy policy OPA evaluation.
 Kernel reads this result and either rejects the request (allow = false) or
 mints an external token incorporating the specified mutations.

fields.name: allow
fields.description:
allow indicates whether the request is permitted.
 When false, kernel rejects the ExternalTokenMint call with PERMISSION_DENIED.

fields.name: url
fields.description:
url, if non-empty, is the resolved destination URL for the upstream request.
 Kernel returns this to the proxy in ExternalTokenMintResponse so the proxy
 forwards to the correct destination. Empty means the proxy uses its own
 DEFAULT_API_ENDPOINT for the service.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTP_OR_HTTPS)

fields.name: reason
fields.description:
reason explains the denial. Returned to the proxy in the denial status.
 Empty when allow = true.

fields.name: append_aud
fields.description:
append_aud contains zero or more audience values to append to the minted
 external token's aud claim. The caller's original aud is always preserved —
 OPA may only add audiences, never replace or remove the original.
 Most policies leave this empty. Set it when the upstream requires a specific
 audience value (e.g. an OIDC client ID or SAML SP entity ID) in addition to
 the caller's existing aud.

fields.name: extra_claims
fields.description:
extra_claims contains additional JWT claims to inject into the minted token.
 Kernel merges these into the token payload alongside the standard claims.
 Existing claims on the caller's token are never removed — only additions
 are permitted to prevent privilege escalation via claim stripping.

fields.name: auth_type
fields.description:
auth_type determines the credential format kernel returns to the proxy.
 TOKEN_TYPE_JWT (default): kernel returns a signed JWT in the response.
 TOKEN_TYPE_SAML: kernel returns a SAML assertion in the response.
 Unset is treated as TOKEN_TYPE_JWT.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_JWT
enum_values.description: TokenTypeJwt represents a JWT token

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_SAML
enum_values.description: TokenTypeSaml represents a SAML token

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_SSH
enum_values.description: TokenTypeSsh represents an SSH token

fields.name: token_use
fields.description:
token_use sets the token_use claim on the minted external token.
 Must be TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL or TOKEN_USE_UNSPECIFIED (both result in
 TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL being stamped). Kernel rejects any other value to
 ensure external tokens can never be replayed against internal services.
 Policies should set this explicitly to TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL to document intent.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description:
TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL marks a token minted by the token authority for use with an external upstream service.
 Internal service auth middleware rejects any token carrying this token_use value,
 preventing a compromised proxy from replaying an externally-minted credential
 against platform-internal services.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE
enum_values.description:
TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE is the long-lived, identity-only Offline Token (OT) held
 by the client daemon on disk. Carries no entitlements (its long TTL would
 make an embedded entitlement snapshot lie). Used as input to mint AT, and to
 self-renew via TokenMint(input=OT, no aud).

Generated by tacplus from spec.opa_eval annotations.

# tacplus Registry

This file is embedded in `registry.json` and describes how to navigate it.

## Overview

This registry describes a tacplus-generated service mesh with:
- **1006** message types across **63** packages
- **631** RPCs across **58** gRPC services
- **56** state boundaries

## Structure

The registry is a recursive `PackageNode` tree. Each node has:
- `name` — short package name
- `full_path` — slash-separated path from root
- `children` — sub-packages
- `proto_packages` — declared protobuf package names represented by a leaf node
- `vservices` — virtual service identities declared by proto files in a leaf node
- `client_dependencies` — declared `grpc_*_client` edges with `surface_kind`
- `types` — message type descriptors (`TypeInfo`)
- `rpcs` — RPC descriptors (`RpcInfo`)
- `boundaries` — state boundary descriptors (`BoundaryInfo`)

Navigate by traversing `children` to reach any package. Directory paths are navigation
labels; use `proto_packages`, `TypeInfo.package`, and `ServiceInfo.package` for
declared protobuf identity.

## Self-Description

The `$schema` field points to `registry.schema.json` (JSON Schema format).
The type definitions under `sys/tacplus` describe this document's own structure:
`PackageNode`, `TypeInfo`, `FieldInfo`, `RpcInfo`, `BoundaryInfo`, `EnumValueInfo`.

## Field Metadata

`FieldInfo` includes protobuf oneof grouping:
- `oneof` — true when the field is a member of a protobuf oneof group
- `oneof_name` — the declared oneof group name

`FieldInfo.constraint_infos` contains machine-readable validation constraints
derived from proto annotations and compiler default bounds. Prefer
`constraint_infos` over parsing the legacy prose strings in `constraints`.

Durable `service_store` messages are surfaced in metadata:
- `TypeInfo.service_store` / `service_store_name` / `service_store_tag`
- `FieldInfo.store_key` — the key field for a service_store value
- `FieldInfo.quorum_write` — field writes require quorum acknowledgement

## VService Metadata

`PackageNode.vservices` lists file-level `(spec.vservice)` identities with
`name`, `id`, and declaring `package`. Hosted vservice RPC surfaces expose their
hosting tag on `ServiceInfo.host_tag`.

## Client Dependencies

`PackageNode.client_dependencies` lists file-level `grpc_s2s_client`,
`grpc_c2s_client`, `grpc_w2s_client`, and `all_grpc_s2s_clients` declarations.
Each edge includes `source_package`, `surface_kind`, `service`,
`target_package`, `target_service`, and `wildcard`.

## Event Topology

`PackageNode.event_publishes` and `PackageNode.event_watches` list validated
actor bindings from `(spec.event_publish)` and `(spec.event_watch)`. Each entry
includes the actor package/message, canonical `topic_ref`, resolved
`event_type_fqn`, broker tag, RPC stem, and derived auth shape.

## RPC Surfaces

`RpcInfo.auth_model` is the primary annotated service model (`s2s`, `c2s`, or
`c2d`). `RpcInfo.surfaces` lists every generated transport/auth surface for an
RPC. Use it when you need additive exposure such as W2S gRPC-over-REST:
`surface_kind` / `auth_model` may be `w2s`, `transport` is `grpc_over_rest`,
and the row carries the W2S HTTP route plus namespace/auth metadata.

## RPC Classification

Every RPC may carry classifier metadata derived from the governed verb registry:
- `auth_model` — primary annotated service model: `s2s`, `c2s`, or `c2d`
- `verb_status` — `classified`, `unclassified`, or `exempt`
- `rpc_verb` / `rpc_noun` — the canonical `Verb<Noun>` split when classification succeeds
- `method_pattern` — the static shape (`GET`, `LIST`, `WATCH`, `CREATE`, `UPDATE`,
  `DELETE`, `ACTION`, `CLIENT_STREAM`, or `BIDI`)
- `access_kind` — `READ` or `WRITE`
- `verb_class` — `core`, `action`, or `agent`
- `entitlement_scopes` — grant scopes that admit the method, ordered broad to narrow
- `retry_policy` — semantic retry/idempotency posture
- `capability_scope` — primary package capability bucket for capability-any expansion
- `verb_definition`, `verb_boundary`, `audit_meaning` — governed dictionary metadata
- `rejected_verbs` — non-canonical verbs that fold to the canonical verb and are rejected
- `folded_to_verb` — canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known
- `allowed_patterns` — patterns this canonical verb may resolve to
- `handler_shape` — `UNARY`, `SERVER_STREAM`, `CLIENT_STREAM`, or `BIDI`

The legacy `category` field is also present for older policy code:
- **ACCESSOR** — read/observe operations (Get, Watch, Query, KeySet, Size, ContainsKey, List, Peek, Subscribe)
- **MUTATOR** — write/modify operations (Set, Put, Delete, Remove, Clear, Publish, Offer, Reload)
- **EXECUTOR** — action/command operations (Assist, Authenticate, Authorize, Evaluate, Exchange, etc.)

Per-service aggregate enum values (`ALL_ACCESSORS`, `ALL_MUTATORS`, `ALL_EXECUTORS`) are available for security policy rules.

## Security Metadata

Each `BoundaryInfo` carries:
- `boundary_callers` — which services can call this boundary cross-namespace

Each `RpcInfo` carries:
- `auth_disabled` — whether authentication is bypassed
- `auth_services` — S2S caller service allowlist when applicable
- `auth_entitled_users` — C2S entitlement-checked user access
- `auth_any_user` — C2S authenticated-user access without entitlement checks
- `auth_model` — primary annotated service model (`s2s`, `c2s`, or `c2d`)
- `target_namespace_field`, `subject_namespace_source`,
  `target_namespace_source`, `target_namespace` — namespace authorization inputs
- `surfaces` — per-transport auth metadata, including derived W2S rows
- `category` — legacy accessor/mutator/executor classification
- `rpc_verb`, `rpc_noun`, `method_pattern`, `access_kind`, `verb_class`,
  `entitlement_scopes`, `retry_policy`, `capability_scope`, `verb_definition`,
  `verb_boundary`, `audit_meaning`, `rejected_verbs`, `allowed_patterns`,
  `handler_shape` — governed verb/pattern metadata when classification succeeds

# tacplus Generated API

This document defines the public API surfaces tacplus generates and the
behavioral guarantees those surfaces provide. `USER.md` explains how to declare
these surfaces in proto and `tacplus.yaml`; `DEVELOPMENT.md` explains how the
compiler preserves them.

The rule of thumb is simple: hand-written service code implements business
logic at the generated handler seam. Everything else that is common across
services or languages is generated and owned by tacplus.

## Generated Surface

For a proto package that declares services, state, stores, or client
dependencies, tacplus emits the full service surface in the full-service
targets (`go`, `rust`, `java`):

| Surface | Contract |
|---|---|
| ServiceManager | Owns startup, identity, config, state-store connection, TLS, generated clients, server wrappers, health, tracing, and shutdown. |
| Handler | The only business-logic seam. Implementers provide handler methods; generated wrappers call them after auth and validation. |
| Service wrappers | Enforce inbound validation, authentication, authorization, namespace policy, tracing/accounting, handler dispatch, outbound validation, and stable status-code mapping. |
| Client managers | Expose typed C2S/W2S/S2S/C2D clients selected by proto annotations and `tacplus.yaml` transport settings, subject to the target language support matrix. |
| State clients | Expose typed read/write/watch access to proto-declared state roots, with imports restricted to generated read-only accessors. |
| Typed disk persistence | Exposes typed snapshot and redo-log persistence for generated store/state types when enabled by the generated service/store config. |
| registry.json | Exposes the normalized semantic IR: types, services, auth metadata, RPC verb/pattern metadata, state roots, projections, annotations, and generated surface metadata. |

No full-service language is the reference implementation. The contract is the
annotated proto model plus the generated API behavior described here.

Client-only targets do not implement the service runtime contract, and split
into two tiers. `swift` and `csharp` are "lite" client targets: they emit C2D,
C2S, and W2S client surfaces, but their W2S is unary-only (HTTP/JSON; no SSE or
WebSocket streaming): a declared streaming method is omitted from the W2S client
(logged; not a generation error, so a mixed service still compiles) and
— unlike the full-client tier — they currently emit no client-side request
validation and no default request deadline. `python` and
`typescript` are full-client targets: they emit every client surface (C2D, C2S,
W2S, and REST) with client-side validation. Both tiers reject S2S clients,
server wrappers, ServiceManager runtime, EventBus runtime, health runtime, SMB
runtime, service state, and service stores loudly, instead of silently producing
partial service code.

## ServiceManager

The ServiceManager (`sm`) is the top-level reachable surface for generated
runtime infrastructure. Generated helpers and wrappers may exist internally, but
application code should reach generated capabilities through `sm`.

The ServiceManager is responsible for:

- loading generated config and runtime environment;
- creating and refreshing identity tokens;
- obtaining and renewing TLS material;
- connecting to the state store and declared service dependencies;
- exposing typed state, store, and service clients;
- installing generated server wrappers around the handler;
- publishing health/readiness and trace/accounting events;
- shutting down owned tasks, streams, and clients.

If a service implementation manually wires raw gRPC servers, auth interceptors,
state-watch loops, bearer headers, or generated transport clients that should be
available through `sm`, that is either a caller bug or a missing generated
surface.

### Certificate Delivery Streams

Generated ServiceManagers own long-lived certificate delivery streams in
full-service targets (`go`, `rust`, `java`). The contract applies to both
auto-TLS (`X509Mint`/`ManageCert`) and SMB member certificate
(`SmbCertService`/`ManageSmbCert`) streams.

Certificate streams are startup-critical until the first usable credential is
installed. After that first credential, they are renewal-critical: failures must
be retried without leaving the service permanently stale or pairing an old
certificate with a new private key. Handlers only install delivered credentials
through the generated handler seam.

Startup follows this state machine:

1. Resolve the authority endpoint for the current attempt.
2. Generate a pending private key and CSR.
3. Open the certificate stream with a cancellable attempt context.
4. Wait for the first delivery.
5. Promote the pending key only after the matching certificate delivery is
   accepted by the generated handler seam.
6. Report startup success only after the first credential has been installed.

Startup attempts use bounded exponential backoff with a shutdown escape. If the
attempt budget is exhausted before first delivery, startup fails loudly.
Shutdown or cancellation exits without reporting a false startup success.

Required failure behavior:

| Case | Generated behavior |
|---|---|
| Authority unreachable before first delivery | Retry with bounded backoff; exhaust budget as startup error. |
| Stream open error before first delivery | Retry with bounded backoff; exhaust budget as startup error. |
| Clean stream end before first delivery | Startup error for that attempt; retry until the startup budget is exhausted. |
| Server error before first delivery | Startup error for that attempt; retry until the startup budget is exhausted. |
| First-delivery handler failure | Fatal startup error; do not retry because local installation failed. |
| Shutdown before first delivery | Exit promptly and do not mark startup successful. |
| Clean stream end after first delivery | Reconnect while running, with backoff and endpoint re-resolution inside the loop. |
| Server error after first delivery | Reconnect while running, with backoff and endpoint re-resolution inside the loop. |
| Renewal handler failure | Log and retry; keep the last active credential. |
| Renewal CSR/key generation failure | Log and retry; keep the last active credential. |

Every renewal attempt uses a pending key distinct from the active key. The
active key must not be replaced at CSR generation time. Promotion is atomic:
generate pending key, send the CSR built from it, receive the matching
certificate chain, invoke the generated handler seam with the pending key and
delivered certificate, and promote pending to active only if the handler returns
success. On stream error, clean stream end, handler failure, cancellation, or
shutdown, the pending key is discarded and the service keeps using the last
active credential until a future renewal succeeds.

Every stream attempt must have a cancellable context or equivalent cancellation
handle. On every exit path, including clean stream end, server error, startup
failure, handler failure, timeout, and shutdown, generated code cancels or
half-closes the stream or call before retrying or returning. Reconnect loops
re-resolve the authority endpoint on every attempt; a certificate stream must
not pin a dead channel, stub, observer, or connection forever after the
authority endpoint changes.

SMB member certificate delivery follows the same state machine and staging
rules. The delivered per-SMB CA certificate is the trust anchor for the
black-box member mesh. The true root CA and any CA private key must not enter
generated black-box runtime configuration. The generated SMB handler seam
receives the delivered member certificate chain, the pending member private key,
and the delivered per-SMB CA certificate; the pending member key is promoted
only after that handler seam succeeds.

The behavioral fixture for this contract drives both auto-TLS and SMB loops
through first delivery success, renewal success, clean end before and after
first delivery, server error before and after first delivery, authority
unreachable, first-delivery handler failure, renewal handler failure, and
shutdown during startup and renewal attempts. Template-level regression tests
pin the state-machine markers where a full runtime fixture is not practical.

The fixture does NOT currently exercise endpoint re-resolution after reconnect
or CSR/key generation failure injection. Reconnect behavior is tested (the loop
does reconnect after post-delivery errors), but re-resolution to a changed
endpoint is not pinned. The contract requires it (see the required failure
table above), and template code implements it, but no behavioral test verifies
it.

## Handler And Wrappers

Handlers are the only generated seam intended for handwritten business logic.
The generated wrapper owns the request pipeline:

1. Decode the proto message.
2. Authenticate and authorize when auth is enabled. This precedes validation so
   an unauthenticated caller cannot drive the validation path or distinguish
   outcomes by the validation errors it returns.
3. Validate inbound request constraints before handler dispatch.
4. Enforce subject/object namespace rules when the proto declares namespace
   fields: a subject may act only at or below its namespace level.
5. Call the handler.
6. Validate each outbound response or stream item before sending it.
7. Map failures to stable generated error/status codes.
8. Emit trace/accounting/health hooks where the generated service surface
   requires them.

Outbound validation applies to user-defined response messages on every
generated full-service send path, including gRPC unary/streaming and W2S
REST/SSE translation. `google.protobuf.*` well-known responses such as
`Empty` carry no tacplus `assert_*` constraints, so generated wrappers pass
them through without a validation call.

**W2S REST/SSE egress validation scope**: the Rust W2S server dispatch
(`rest_dispatch.rs.tmpl`) validates both unary responses and SSE stream items
before sending. Go and Java W2S servers validate outbound messages through
their gRPC wrapper pipeline (the REST surface is implemented as a translation
layer atop gRPC, so gRPC egress validation covers it). Python and TypeScript
are client-only targets and do not host a W2S server.

Auth-disabled methods skip token lookup and authorization but still validate
messages. Auth-enabled methods must not reach the handler without a valid token
and a satisfied authorization decision.

## Transport Surfaces

Service shape is declared in proto. `tacplus.yaml` only chooses which transport
surfaces to emit for the current package and language.

| Surface | Meaning | Transport |
|---|---|---|
| C2S | client to service | native gRPC |
| W2S | web to service | gRPC-over-HTTP/REST surface suitable for browser callers |
| S2S | service to service | native gRPC with service identity tokens |
| C2D | client to daemon | local IPC gRPC, such as Unix domain sockets or named pipes |

C2S and W2S are not mutually exclusive for full-service targets. A native/server
package may enable either or both. Browser web apps should enable W2S and should
not enable C2S.

C2D is a local daemon IPC surface; it does not introduce SMN/SMB mesh work.
The lite client targets (`swift`, `csharp`) emit C2D, C2S, and W2S clients
(their W2S is unary-only — streaming methods are emitted as throwing stubs);
the full-client targets (`python`, `typescript`) additionally emit REST clients.

C2D server wrappers skip token authentication by design: the auth boundary is
the socket permission (filesystem ACL / named-pipe DACL), not a bearer token.
The generated wrapper still validates request/response constraints and runs the
full handler pipeline; only the token-lookup and authorization steps are
bypassed. This is implemented via the `IsC2D` flag on the service descriptor.

### Client Send Contract

Generated clients validate before sending. Auth scope depends on the call
shape:

- **Unary / server-streaming**: a fresh token is obtained per CALL; if the
  identity manager cannot provide one, the call fails before leaving the
  process.
- **Client-streaming / bidi**: auth is STREAM-OPEN scoped — exactly one token
  is attached to the stream headers when the stream opens (gRPC metadata
  cannot change mid-stream). There is deliberately no per-send token
  preflight: it would mint a token the server never sees while still being
  able to fail a legitimate send. A server that rejects an expired stream
  credential terminates the stream; the generated reconnect paths (e.g.
  EventBus subscribers) obtain a fresh token per reconnect attempt.

Auth-disabled calls bypass token lookup.

Generated mutation helpers do not retry by default unless the generated API
explicitly marks the operation as safe. Read-like helpers may use generated
retry/backoff policy.

## State And Store Access

A message annotated as service state becomes a typed state root. The generated
surface includes:

- a state service with typed Get/Set/Watch/Delete-style RPCs for the declared
  boundaries;
- typed state clients surfaced from the ServiceManager;
- generated import accessors for read-only cross-service state imports;
- server-side enforcement that imports cannot write through raw RPCs;
- view services for declared read-only unions across compatible roots;
- topic, queue, command, persistence, and eviction behavior declared by proto
  annotations.

Services own their state. Other services access exported state through declared
imports and generated read-only accessors, not by manually dialing backing state
services.

## Typed Disk Persistence

Typed disk persistence is the generated disk analogue of typed HTTP clients:
code reads and writes proto types with generated serialization and validation,
not raw JSON or ad hoc file I/O.

The generated contract is:

- JSON plus newline framing only; no alternate on-disk format;
- write paths use generated `ToJSON` helpers;
- read paths use generated `FromJSON` helpers and then `Validate`;
- invalid data on read fails closed;
- single-writer, single-process, local-filesystem only;
- same-directory atomic rename and file/parent-directory fsync for replacement
  writes;
- archive rotation for replaced or compacted files;
- redo logs append newline-delimited records and compact by snapshotting the
  latest keyed state;
- restore handles active, temporary, and in-progress promoted files without
  silently dropping a committed baseline.

The ServiceManager owns scheduled redo-log lifecycle when the init-time
`grpcconfig.Config.disk_persistence` setting is present. Generated
ServiceManagers open one redo-log handle per hosted keyed `service_store`,
expose those handles to service code, and run deterministic per-store roll
schedulers. This setting is not hot-reloaded; service code should append through
the ServiceManager-owned handles and should not run its own backup loop for
generated stores.

## Collection RPCs

Collection-returning RPCs are explicit. A multi-result read declares a
`method_collection` mode and bound; tacplus derives transport tier, flow
control, and public handler/client shapes from that declaration.

A unary response whose only meaningful field is one repeated result field is
the Tier-1 collection convention and must be annotated. Tacplus rejects that
shape when `method_collection` is absent because there is no safe way to infer
bounds, transport tier, or public handler/client shape from proto alone.
Composite responses that happen to contain repeated nested fields are not
treated as collection reads unless annotated.

### Modes

| Mode | Contract |
|---|---|
| SNAPSHOT | Finite point-in-time result. Requires a positive `max_items`; terminates. |
| WATCH | Open-ended change stream. Requires an explicit `from_revision`; does not self-terminate. |
| PAGE | Unary, client-driven window over an ordered set. Requires `order_by` and a positive `default_page_size`; the client resumes with an opaque `page_token`. |

An unbounded non-async read is invalid. If a read is unbounded, it is a WATCH.

### Snapshot Tiers

Tacplus computes `max_items * item_bytes` and selects a delivery tier:

| Tier | Wire shape | Handler surface | Client surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | unary response with exactly one repeated field | materialized collection | materialized collection |
| Tier 2 | server-streaming items | materialized collection | materialized collection |
| Tier 3 | server-streaming items | lazy producer/iterator | lazy iterator/stream |

Tier-2 and Tier-3 proto methods are ordinary gRPC server-streaming methods. The
streamed message is the item. Tier-1 proto methods are ordinary unary methods
whose response contains exactly one repeated field.

### WATCH Contract

A WATCH proto method is an ordinary server-streaming RPC whose response is an
author-declared envelope:

- `snapshot_item` entries establish the initial state;
- `snapshot_done` carries the revision at which that snapshot is complete;
- `delta` entries carry later changes;
- stale `from_revision` returns `OUT_OF_RANGE`, prompting the client to relist.

The handler returns a language-appropriate `WatchSource` shape containing scope,
snapshot producer, revision, and change producer. The generated wrapper owns
envelope framing, replay-ring lookup, relist behavior, teardown, and flow
control. The replay ring lives in a shared per-language collection runtime lib,
keyed by scope and bounded by `replay_depth`.

### PAGE Contract

A PAGE proto method is an ordinary **unary** RPC. The request carries the filter
fields plus `int32 page_size` and `string page_token`; the response carries
exactly one `repeated` items field, `string next_page_token`, and an optional
`int64 total_count`. Generation rejects a request that declares `page_token` /
`page_size` (or a response with `next_page_token`) but lacks
`COLLECTION_MODE_PAGE` — otherwise it would silently degrade to an unbounded
unary with no page ceiling.

The generated wrapper owns the page mechanics; the handler is a keyset producer:

- `page_token` decodes to a keyset cursor (the `order_by` key of the last row).
  A malformed token is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` — never a silent reset to the first
  page (which would skip rows and read as success).
- The effective page size is `page_size` when positive, else `default_page_size`,
  clamped to the trust tier's `MaxPageSize` (`Ceilings.MaxItems`: 100 anon /
  10k C2S-auth / 1M S2S). This is the per-call row ceiling that SNAPSHOT's
  `max_items` provides statically and that streaming reads lack.
- The handler receives `PageParams{limit, after}` plus the request and returns a
  `Page{items, nextAfter, total}` (`total = -1` means "unknown", not "empty").
  The wrapper encodes `nextAfter` into `next_page_token` (empty on the last
  page) and sets `total_count` only when the handler computed it.

The `page_token` is opaque, versioned, and **byte-identical across all
full-service backends** — base64url(no pad) of `{"v":1,"k":[...]}` over the
`order_by` key — so a token minted against one backend decodes on any other.
Pages are best-effort keyset over `order_by` (stable when the sort key is
monotonic/immutable); they are not a point-in-time snapshot unless the handler
bakes a revision into the key.

Each language exposes two client seams: an explicit single-page call
(`{Method}Page` → items + `next_page_token` + total) and an auto-pager (the
natural method name) that follows `next_page_token` until exhausted —
`iter.Seq2` (Go), an async generator (TypeScript), an async generator (Python),
a `futures::Stream` (Rust), and a lazy `Iterator` (Java). The auto-pager
advances the token on a request clone, so the caller's request is not mutated.

### Flow Control And Teardown

Generated stream wrappers must respect transport backpressure and deterministic
cleanup. Java uses `ServerCallStreamObserver` readiness hooks. TypeScript uses
`write()` backpressure and `drain`. Go, Rust, and Python rely on their native
stream/cancellation semantics.

Idle-timeout backstop — scope. The generated idle-timeout backstop applies to
**long-lived WATCH streams**: the replay Ring waits for the next delta and, if
none arrives within the caller's trust-tier `STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, ends the
stream with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` — a living query must not pin a connection
forever while idle. It does **not** apply to finite **Tier-3 SNAPSHOT cursors**:
a cursor is a bounded pull over a materialized result set, so its teardown is
driven by exhaustion, client cancellation, or the request context deadline, not
a server-side idle timer. (The cursor producer is a synchronous pull — an
`iter.Seq2` / equivalent — that cannot be preempted mid-`Next` without leaking
the producer goroutine, so a per-item idle timer is deliberately not generated;
a handler whose producer can wedge must honor the context itself.)

## EventBus Topics

EventBus participation in generated service runtimes is declared, never
inferred. A topic is a message
carrying `(spec.service_event)` (with `tag` naming the broker service) plus a
field carrying `(spec.topic) = true`. Producers and consumers declare
`(spec.event_publish)` / `(spec.event_watch)` with a `topic_ref` in the
canonical format, parsed from the right so dotted packages work:

```text
<proto-package>.<topic-message>.<topic-field>
e.g. claudesensor.AgenticCodeEventBus.event_stream
```

Full-service generation validates every `topic_ref` before emitting code: it must match the
grammar, resolve to exactly one package/message/field, point at a
`(spec.service_event)` message and a `(spec.topic)` field, and preserve the
field's protobuf type as the event type. Ambiguity or absence fails generation.

Typed EventBus Subscribe responses use a metadata-bearing envelope, not a bare
event payload. Field 1 is the record metadata and field 2 is the typed event
payload. The metadata wire fields are stable across languages:
`key = 1`, `topic = 2`, `partition = 3`, `offset = 4`, and
`timestamp = 5`.

EventBus publish/watch RPCs are derived RPCs, and **auth uses the standard
method auth model, not an EventBus-specific vocabulary**: the
`event_publish`/`event_watch` annotations carry the normal `method_s2s` /
`method_c2s` shapes, and generation copies that policy onto the derived RPC's
metadata exactly as if hand-authored. Topic declarations are collected from all
loaded descriptors, but publish/watch bindings attach only to the **current
actor's own protos** — importing a proto never makes a service (or the broker
itself) a producer or subscriber.

## RPC Patterns And Verbs

Every RPC resolves to exactly one pattern from a closed set, with one static
access kind: `GET` (READ) · `LIST` (READ; SNAPSHOT or PAGE) · `WATCH` (READ) ·
`CREATE`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` (WRITE) · `ACTION` · `CLIENT_STREAM` · `BIDI`
(declared access, default WRITE). One method = one verb = one access kind;
branching a method's meaning on input is an architectural-norm violation (see
`DEVELOPMENT.md`).

RPC names are `Verb<Noun>` (PascalCase, verb first) against a **closed verb
registry**. A verb exists only if the operation cannot be expressed as
Get/List/Watch/Create/Update/Delete without losing meaning (the fold test);
synonyms fold to canonicals and are rejected:

- **Core (6)**: Get, List (replaces Search/Query/Find), Watch, Create, Update,
  Delete.
- **Action (14)**: Mint, Revoke, Authorize, Send, Publish, Subscribe, Broker,
  Execute, Cancel, Retry, Reset, Ping, Proxy, Merge. `Subscribe` and `Broker`
  are canonical action verbs (not folded to `Watch`); the messaging verbs are
  `Send`/`Publish`/`Subscribe`/`Broker`. Stateful vs stateless rule:
  `Create`/`Delete` for stored resources; `Mint`/`Revoke` for self-contained
  credentials (a JWT is `MintToken`, never `CreateSession`). Protocol-mandated
  URL paths (OAuth/OIDC/SAML) live on `rest_path`/`acs_path`; the *name*
  conforms to the registry.
- **AI/Agent (7)**: Generate, Embed, Classify, Rank, Assist, Guard, Evaluate —
  all under the `AGENT` entitlement scope. Fold rules: Summarize/Translate/
  Rewrite/Redact→Generate; Moderate/Detect→Classify; Rerank→Rank;
  Plan/Critique→Assist; semantic Search→List.

The registry is governed: core/action verbs admit rarely under strict review;
agent verbs have a lighter bar but the registry stays closed. The authored
compiler dictionary is `pkg/internal/common/verbs/registry.json`; generated
service semantic output lands in the build artifact `registry.json` `RpcInfo`
(see Tracing And Registry).
`EnforceVerbs` is part of descriptor parsing for generated-auth surfaces:
non-canonical verbs, folded synonyms, noun-first names, and
verb/pattern/cardinality mismatches fail generation before registry,
entitlement, or REST metadata can be emitted. Full design genealogy:
`../archive/RPC_PATTERNS_AND_VERBS_PLAN.md`.

## Auth And Namespace Policy

Auth policy is declared in proto service and method annotations. Generated code
performs token verification, service/user authorization, entitlement checks, and
namespace enforcement before handler dispatch.

Subject namespace and object namespace are distinct. When both are declared, the
subject namespace must be at or above the object namespace. Generated code must
deny namespace-mismatched calls before the handler. Channels with auth disabled
do not perform token lookup but still validate message constraints.

## SPIFFE Identity

All SPIFFE identity construction, parsing, and comparison goes through the
generated `sys/spiffe` — no generated code or downstream service formats or
splits `spiffe://...` strings by hand.

**Trust domain.** The URI authority: a single globally unique instance name
containing no `/` (e.g. `example.com`). Configured per deployment
(`spiffe_trust_domain`); a missing or malformed value fails loudly — there is
no default.

**URI layout** (typed, self-describing — the kind is recoverable from fixed
tags, no side channel needed):

```text
spiffe://<trust_domain>/
  system/<location...>/services/<service>[/workloads/<child>...]
  tenants/<tenant>/users/<user>
  tenants/<tenant>/workspaces/<workspace>...
  tenants/<tenant>/...[/clients/<client>]
  tenants/<tenant>/...[/credentials/<kind>/<id>]
  tenants/<tenant>/...[/data/<kind>/<id>]
```

`/system` holds infrastructure/service identities; `/tenants` holds
tenant-scoped principals and resources. The `<location...>` tiers between
`/system/` and `services` are opaque and variable-arity (the parser keys off
the `services` tag). Reserved tags (`system`, `tenants`, `services`,
`workloads`, `users`, `workspaces`, `clients`, `credentials`, `data`) are
rejected as namespace segments at every depth.

**Segment grammar**: `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`. Empty segments, separators,
traversal, query/fragment, control characters, and encoded separators are
rejected. **Reject by default; never sanitize-and-accept.** Richer external
identifiers go through `opaque_segment(kind, value)` (SHA-256 over
`kind‖0x1F‖NFC(value)`, truncated to 160 bits, lowercase base32 no-pad) —
byte-identical across supported target surfaces.

**Service identity and matching.** The canonical service SPIFFE ID —
`spiffe://<td>/system[/<loc>...]/services/<svc>` — is what the cert minter
emits as the X509 URI SAN and what the generated go/rust/java peer verifiers
require (parsed via sys/spiffe; `SubjectKind == Service`, trust domain equal,
service label equal). S2S `auth_services` checks match on the
location-agnostic `service_path()` (the bare service label, location tiers
stripped), so the same service matches in any cloud/account/az/cluster.

**Token claims.** The SPIFFE ID is *derived* from claims, never carried as a
claim: `namespace` is the authorization-tree path; `sub` is the stable
principal id (not a URI); `sub_type` ∈ {service, workload, user, client,
external}; `azp` is the attestation context (kernel/oauth/saml/cloud-auth) —
attestation is never encoded in the subject path, so the same human in the
same tenant role has the same subject regardless of login method.
`/tenants/<t>/users/<u>` is a tenant-scoped role, not the global human; the
person is correlated only via the stable IDP `sub`. External tokens are
rejected by generated internal auth.

Full design rationale and decision record:
`../archive/SPIFFE_IDENTITY_NORMALIZATION_PLAN.md`.

## Validation And Errors

Every generated language enforces the same field constraints, default collection
bounds, oneof scalar string/bytes bounds, maximum message nesting depth, enum
vocabulary, and message validation semantics. Generated validators reject
nested message graphs deeper than 24 levels and reject enum numeric values not
declared in the proto. A declared zero/sentinel enum value is allowed unless
`assert_enum_defined` is present. Generated code should fail closed for invalid
proto shapes, invalid runtime config, invalid tokens, unsafe transport setup,
and failed validation.

Generated types and wrappers should expose tacplus structured errors/status
codes rather than language-specific exception behavior at public seams.

## Tracing And Registry

Generated service wrappers emit typed trace/accounting data where the surface
requires it. Request handlers are responsible for propagating non-empty
`trace_id` fields into downstream requests they create.

`registry.json` is the machine-readable semantic IR. Service-local generators
must read `registry.json`, not parse proto files directly, when they need
tacplus semantics such as projections, store metadata, auth metadata, or
generated surface information.

For generated-auth RPCs, `RpcInfo` includes both transport/auth metadata and
governed classification metadata. A **C2S** generated-auth method that cannot
classify fails generation (the external surface is strict). An **S2S** or
**C2D** generated-auth method that cannot classify does NOT fail generation:
its `RpcInfo` is emitted with `verb_status = "unclassified"` (or `"exempt"`
when the method carries no auth model at all), the folded verb recorded in
`folded_to_verb`, and the governed classification fields (`rpc_verb`,
`rpc_noun`, `method_pattern`, `access_kind`, …) left empty. Internal surfaces
are looser because store/infra RPCs legitimately fall outside the C2S verb
dictionary; the recorded `verb_status` is the signal, not a hard failure. When
classification succeeds:

- `rpc_verb` and `rpc_noun` from the canonical `Verb<Noun>` split.
- `method_pattern`: `GET`, `LIST`, `WATCH`, `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`,
  `ACTION`, `CLIENT_STREAM`, or `BIDI`.
- `access_kind`: `READ` or `WRITE`.
- `verb_class`: `core`, `action`, or `agent`.
- `entitlement_scopes`: grant scopes that admit the method, ordered broad to
  narrow.
- `retry_policy`: `READ_ONLY`, `WATCH_RECONNECT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_REQUIRED`, or
  `NO_GENERATED_AUTO_RETRY`.
- `capability_scope`: primary package capability bucket for capability-any
  expansion (`READ`, `WRITE`, `WATCH`, `PAGE`, or `AGENT`).
- `verb_definition`, `verb_boundary`, and `audit_meaning`: governed dictionary
  metadata for documentation, review, and operator/security surfaces.
- `rejected_verbs`: known non-canonical verbs that fold to `rpc_verb` and are
  rejected by generation.
- `allowed_patterns`: method patterns the canonical verb may resolve to.
- `handler_shape`: `UNARY`, `SERVER_STREAM`, `CLIENT_STREAM`, or `BIDI`.

The root `entitlement_grants` array is the generated grant catalog for C2S
authorization tooling. It includes entitlement-checked C2S methods, not
`auth_disabled` or `auth_any_user` methods. Exact grants identify one
package/service/RPC token. Wildcard grants such as `PACKAGE_ANY`,
`PACKAGE_READ_ANY`, `PACKAGE_WATCH_ANY`, and `PACKAGE_PAGE_ANY` are convenience
values whose `expands_to` list contains the exact grants they imply. Runtime
authorizers should authorize against exact grants after expansion; wildcard
values are not runtime magic.

Empty classification fields are invalid for **C2S** generated-auth surfaces
(they hard-fail generation). On S2S/C2D surfaces empty fields are permitted and
accompanied by a non-`classified` `verb_status`, as described above. Consumers
should read the generated fields (and `verb_status`) rather than inventing a
second classifier.

## Parity

A generated API is complete only when behavior is equivalent across the
supported languages for the same proto model. Parity is measured against proto
annotations, semantic registry metadata, generated-contract tests, and
soundness checks, not against any single language implementation.
